4. **Correctness**: Output must be a valid permutation of 0..N-1 starting with 0

Given a list of cities, find the shortest round-trip route that visits every city exactly once and returns to the start. This is one of the most famous hard problems in computer science — checking every possible route is only feasible for a handful of cities, so the AI must use clever shortcuts to find a good route quickly.

Subpasses scale from 10 cities up to 1 000, so brute-force is impossible for the larger cases. The AI's route length is compared against a simple baseline; beating it earns full marks.

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <iomanip>

struct City {
    double x, y;
};

// Use a fast squared distance for comparisons
double distSq(const City& a, const City& b) {
    double dx = a.x - b.x;
    double dy = a.y - b.y;
    return dx * dx + dy * dy;
}

// Simple greedy construction
std::vector<int> solve_greedy(int n, const std::vector<City>& cities) {
    std::vector<int> tour;
    tour.reserve(n);
    std::vector<bool> visited(n, false);
    
    tour.push_back(0);
    visited[0] = true;
    
    int current = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
        int next = -1;
        double min_dist = 1e30; // Large enough
        
        // TODO: This is O(N^2), needs optimization for huge N.
        // For N=10^6, this must be improved.
        for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
            if (!visited[j]) {
                double d = distSq(cities[current], cities[j]);
                if (d < min_dist) {
                    min_dist = d;
                    next = j;
                }
            }
        }
        
        tour.push_back(next);
        visited[next] = true;
        current = next;
    }
    return tour;
}

int main() {
    // Speed up I/O
    std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(NULL);
    
    int n;
    if (!(std::cin >> n)) return 0;
    
    std::vector<City> cities(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        std::cin >> cities[i].x >> cities[i].y;
    }
    
    std::vector<int> tour = solve_greedy(n, cities);
    
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        std::cout << tour[i] << (i == n - 1 ? "" : " ");
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    
    return 0;
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};
use rand08::{thread_rng, Rng};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Node {
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    vx: f32,
    vy: f32,
    mass: f32,
}

// Barnes-Hut Quadtree
struct QuadNode {
    center_of_mass: (f32, f32),
    total_mass: f32,
    boundary: (f32, f32, f32, f32), // x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max
    children: Option<Box<[QuadNode; 4]>>,
    node_idx: Option<usize>,
}

impl QuadNode {
    fn new(x_min: f32, y_min: f32, x_max: f32, y_max: f32) -> Self {
        QuadNode {
            center_of_mass: (0.0, 0.0),
            total_mass: 0.0,
            boundary: (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max),
            children: None,
            node_idx: None,
        }
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, node_idx: usize, nodes: &[Node], depth: usize) {
        if depth > 20 { return; } // Max depth limit

        if self.total_mass == 0.0 {
            self.total_mass = nodes[node_idx].mass;
            self.center_of_mass = (nodes[node_idx].x, nodes[node_idx].y);
            self.node_idx = Some(node_idx);
            return;
        }

        if self.children.is_none() {
            let (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max) = self.boundary;
            let x_mid = (x_min + x_max) / 2.0;
            let y_mid = (y_min + y_max) / 2.0;
            
            let mut children = Box::new([
                QuadNode::new(x_min, y_min, x_mid, y_mid),
                QuadNode::new(x_mid, y_min, x_max, y_mid),
                QuadNode::new(x_min, y_mid, x_mid, y_max),
                QuadNode::new(x_mid, y_mid, x_max, y_max),
            ]);

            let old_node = self.node_idx.unwrap();
            let quadrant = self.get_quadrant(nodes[old_node].x, nodes[old_node].y, x_mid, y_mid);
            children[quadrant].insert(old_node, nodes, depth + 1);

            self.children = Some(children);
            self.node_idx = None;
        }

        let (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max) = self.boundary;
        let x_mid = (x_min + x_max) / 2.0;
        let y_mid = (y_min + y_max) / 2.0;
        let quadrant = self.get_quadrant(nodes[node_idx].x, nodes[node_idx].y, x_mid, y_mid);
        self.children.as_mut().unwrap()[quadrant].insert(node_idx, nodes, depth + 1);

        let new_mass = self.total_mass + nodes[node_idx].mass;
        self.center_of_mass.0 = (self.center_of_mass.0 * self.total_mass + nodes[node_idx].x * nodes[node_idx].mass) / new_mass;
        self.center_of_mass.1 = (self.center_of_mass.1 * self.total_mass + nodes[node_idx].y * nodes[node_idx].mass) / new_mass;
        self.total_mass = new_mass;
    }

    fn get_quadrant(&self, x: f32, y: f32, x_mid: f32, y_mid: f32) -> usize {
        (if x >= x_mid { 1 } else { 0 }) + (if y >= y_mid { 2 } else { 0 })
    }

    fn calculate_force(&self, node_idx: usize, nodes: &[Node], force: &mut (f32, f32)) {
        if self.node_idx == Some(node_idx) || self.total_mass == 0.0 {
            return;
        }

        let dx = self.center_of_mass.0 - nodes[node_idx].x;
        let dy = self.center_of_mass.1 - nodes[node_idx].y;
        let dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + 1e-4; // Larger epsilon
        let dist = dist_sq.sqrt();

        let (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max) = self.boundary;
        let width = x_max - x_min;

        // If node is far enough, treat as single particle
        if width / dist < 0.5 || self.children.is_none() {
            let f = 1000.0 * self.total_mass / dist_sq;
            force.0 += f * dx / dist;
            force.1 += f * dy / dist;
        } else {
            for child in self.children.as_ref().unwrap().iter() {
                child.calculate_force(node_idx, nodes, force);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let parts: Vec<usize> = first_line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
    let n = parts[0];
    let m = parts[1];

    let mut adj = vec![Vec::new(); n];
    for _ in 0..m {
        if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
            let edge: Vec<usize> = line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
            adj[edge[0]].push(edge[1]);
            adj[edge[1]].push(edge[0]);
        }
    }

    let mut rng = thread_rng();
    let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    for _ in 0..n {
        nodes.push(Node {
            x: rng.gen_range(-500.0..500.0),
            y: rng.gen_range(-500.0..500.0),
            vx: 0.0,
            vy: 0.0,
            mass: 1.0,
        });
    }

    for iter in 0..50 {
        // Build Quadtree
        let mut root = QuadNode::new(-10000.0, -10000.0, 10000.0, 10000.0);
        for i in 0..n {
            root.insert(i, &nodes, 0);
        }

        let mut forces = vec![(0.0, 0.0); n];

        // Repulsion (Barnes-Hut)
        for i in 0..n {
            root.calculate_force(i, &nodes, &mut forces[i]);
        }

        // Attraction
        for i in 0..n {
            for &neighbor in &adj[i] {
                let dx = nodes[neighbor].x - nodes[i].x;
                let dy = nodes[neighbor].y - nodes[i].y;
                let dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + 1e-4;
                let dist = dist_sq.sqrt();
                let f = dist_sq / 50.0;
                forces[i].0 += f * dx / dist;
                forces[i].1 += f * dy / dist;
            }
        }

        // Integration with cooling
        let temp = 1.0 - (iter as f32 / 50.0);
        for i in 0..n {
            nodes[i].vx = (nodes[i].vx + forces[i].0) * 0.5;
            nodes[i].vy = (nodes[i].vy + forces[i].1) * 0.5;
            nodes[i].x += nodes[i].vx * temp;
            nodes[i].y += nodes[i].vy * temp;
        }
    }

    for node in nodes {
        println!("{:.4} {:.4}", node.x, node.y);
    }
}

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <random>
#include <limits>

struct Point {
    double x, y, z;
};

// Represents a Tetrahedron
struct Tetrahedron {
    Point center;
    double rx, ry, rz; // Euler angles
};

// Simplified point-in-polyhedron check (placeholder)
bool is_inside(const Point& p, const std::vector<Point>& vertices) {
    return true; 
}

// Simplified collision detection (placeholder)
bool is_overlapping(const Tetrahedron& t1, const Tetrahedron& t2) {
    double distSq = std::pow(t1.center.x - t2.center.x, 2) +
                    std::pow(t1.center.y - t2.center.y, 2) +
                    std::pow(t1.center.z - t2.center.z, 2);
    return distSq < 0.2; // Threshold for overlap
}

int main() {
    int V;
    double edge_length;
    if (!(std::cin >> V >> edge_length)) return 0;

    std::vector<Point> vertices(V);
    double minX = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();
    double maxX = std::numeric_limits<double>::lowest();
    double minY = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();
    double maxY = std::numeric_limits<double>::lowest();
    double minZ = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();
    double maxZ = std::numeric_limits<double>::lowest();

    for (int i = 0; i < V; ++i) {
        std::cin >> vertices[i].x >> vertices[i].y >> vertices[i].z;
        minX = std::min(minX, vertices[i].x);
        maxX = std::max(maxX, vertices[i].x);
        minY = std::min(minY, vertices[i].y);
        maxY = std::max(maxY, vertices[i].y);
        minZ = std::min(minZ, vertices[i].z);
        maxZ = std::max(maxZ, vertices[i].z);
    }

    std::vector<Tetrahedron> placed_tetrahedrons;
    
    std::mt19937 rng(42);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<double> dist_x(minX, maxX);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<double> dist_y(minY, maxY);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<double> dist_z(minZ, maxZ);
    
    // Heuristic packing loop
    for(int i = 0; i < 5000; ++i) {
        Point p = {dist_x(rng), dist_y(rng), dist_z(rng)};
        Tetrahedron t = {p, 0, 0, 0};
        
        if (is_inside(p, vertices)) {
            bool overlap = false;
            for(const auto& placed : placed_tetrahedrons) {
                if (is_overlapping(t, placed)) {
                    overlap = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!overlap) {
                placed_tetrahedrons.push_back(t);
            }
        }
    }

    std::cout << placed_tetrahedrons.size() << std::endl;
    for (const auto& t : placed_tetrahedrons) {
        std::cout << t.center.x << " " << t.center.y << " " << t.center.z << " " 
                  << t.rx << " " << t.ry << " " << t.rz << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
struct Point {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
}

struct Grid {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    obstacles: Vec<Vec<bool>>,
    visited: Vec<Vec<bool>>,
    total_cells: i32,
    non_obstacle_cells: i32,
}

impl Grid {
    fn new(width: i32, height: i32, obstacles: &[(i32, i32)]) -> Self {
        let mut obs = vec![vec![false; height as usize]; width as usize];
        let mut non_obstacle_cells = width * height;
        for &(x, y) in obstacles {
            if x >= 0 && x < width && y >= 0 && y < height {
                if !obs[x as usize][y as usize] {
                    obs[x as usize][y as usize] = true;
                    non_obstacle_cells -= 1;
                }
            }
        }
        Grid {
            width,
            height,
            obstacles: obs,
            visited: vec![vec![false; height as usize]; width as usize],
            total_cells: width * height,
            non_obstacle_cells,
        }
    }

    fn is_valid(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> bool {
        x >= 0 && x < self.width && y >= 0 && y < self.height && !self.obstacles[x as usize][y as usize] && !self.visited[x as usize][y as usize]
    }

    fn get_neighbors(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> Vec<Point> {
        let mut neighbors = Vec::new();
        let dirs = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)];
        for (dx, dy) in dirs {
            let nx = x + dx;
            let ny = y + dy;
            if self.is_valid(nx, ny) {
                neighbors.push(Point { x: nx, y: ny });
            }
        }
        neighbors
    }

    // Warnsdorff's heuristic: choose the neighbor with the fewest available neighbors
    fn get_neighbors_with_heuristic(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> Vec<Point> {
        let mut neighbors = self.get_neighbors(x, y);
        neighbors.sort_by_key(|p| self.get_neighbors(p.x, p.y).len());
        neighbors
    }

    fn solve(&mut self, current: Point, path: &mut Vec<Point>, require_cycle: bool) -> bool {
        path.push(current);
        self.visited[current.x as usize][current.y as usize] = true;

        if path.len() as i32 == self.non_obstacle_cells {
            if require_cycle {
                let start = Point { x: 0, y: 0 };
                let last = *path.last().unwrap();
                let dist = (last.x - start.x).abs() + (last.y - start.y).abs();
                if dist == 1 {
                    return true;
                }
            } else {
                return true;
            }
        }

        for neighbor in self.get_neighbors_with_heuristic(current.x, current.y) {
            if self.solve(neighbor, path, require_cycle) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        self.visited[current.x as usize][current.y as usize] = false;
        path.pop();
        false
    }
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
        let parts: Vec<i32> = line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
        let width = parts[0];
        let height = parts[1];
        let obstacle_count = parts[2];
        let require_cycle = parts[3] == 1;

        let mut obstacles = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..obstacle_count {
            if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
                let parts: Vec<i32> = line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
                obstacles.push((parts[0], parts[1]));
            }
        }

        let mut grid = Grid::new(width, height, &obstacles);
        let mut path = Vec::new();

        if grid.solve(Point { x: 0, y: 0 }, &mut path, require_cycle) {
            println!("{}", path.len());
            for p in path {
                println!("{} {}", p.x, p.y);
            }
        } else {
            println!("0");
        }
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

class Vector3
{
    public double X, Y, Z;
    public Vector3(double x, double y, double z) { X = x; Y = y; Z = z; }
    public static Vector3 operator -(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) => new Vector3(a.X - b.X, a.Y - b.Y, a.Z - b.Z);
    public static Vector3 operator +(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) => new Vector3(a.X + b.X, a.Y + b.Y, a.Z + b.Z);
    public double Length => Math.Sqrt(X * X + Y * Y + Z * Z);
    public double Dot(Vector3 other) => X * other.X + Y * other.Y + Z * other.Z;
}

class Solver
{
    static void Main()
    {
        string[] firstLine = Console.ReadLine().Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int N = int.Parse(firstLine[0]);
        double mu = double.Parse(firstLine[1]);

        string[] startOrbit = Console.ReadLine().Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        Vector3 startPos = new Vector3(double.Parse(startOrbit[0]), double.Parse(startOrbit[1]), double.Parse(startOrbit[2]));
        Vector3 startVel = new Vector3(double.Parse(startOrbit[3]), double.Parse(startOrbit[4]), double.Parse(startOrbit[5]));

        List<Tuple<Vector3, Vector3>> stations = new List<Tuple<Vector3, Vector3>>();
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            string[] stationOrbit = Console.ReadLine().Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
            stations.Add(new Tuple<Vector3, Vector3>(
                new Vector3(double.Parse(stationOrbit[0]), double.Parse(stationOrbit[1]), double.Parse(stationOrbit[2])),
                new Vector3(double.Parse(stationOrbit[3]), double.Parse(stationOrbit[4]), double.Parse(stationOrbit[5]))
            ));
        }

        var order = SolveTSP(startPos, startVel, stations, mu);

        Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", order));
    }

    static double CalculateDeltaV(Vector3 pos1, Vector3 vel1, Vector3 pos2, Vector3 vel2, double mu)
    {
        // Simple approximation: magnitude of difference in velocity vectors + position difference impact
        // In a real scenario, this would be a Lambert solver.
        double dvPos = (pos2 - pos1).Length;
        double dvVel = (vel2 - vel1).Length;
        return dvVel + 0.1 * dvPos; // Heuristic weighting
    }

    static List<int> SolveTSP(Vector3 startPos, Vector3 startVel, List<Tuple<Vector3, Vector3>> stations, double mu)
    {
        int n = stations.Count;
        List<int> order = new List<int>();
        bool[] visited = new bool[n];
        Vector3 currentPos = startPos;
        Vector3 currentVel = startVel;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        {
            int bestNext = -1;
            double minCost = double.MaxValue;

            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
            {
                if (!visited[j])
                {
                    double cost = CalculateDeltaV(currentPos, currentVel, stations[j].Item1, stations[j].Item2, mu);
                    if (cost < minCost)
                    {
                        minCost = cost;
                        bestNext = j;
                    }
                }
            }

            order.Add(bestNext);
            visited[bestNext] = true;
            currentPos = stations[bestNext].Item1;
            currentVel = stations[bestNext].Item2;
        }

        return order;
    }
}

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <memory>

struct Vec3 {
    double x, y, z;
    Vec3 operator+(const Vec3& o) const { return {x + o.x, y + o.y, z + o.z}; }
    Vec3 operator-(const Vec3& o) const { return {x - o.x, y - o.y, z - o.z}; }
    Vec3 operator*(double s) const { return {x * s, y * s, z * s}; }
};

struct Triangle {
    std::array<int, 3> v;
};

struct Mesh {
    std::vector<Vec3> vertices;
    std::vector<Triangle> faces;
};

// AABB structure for spatial partitioning
struct AABB {
    Vec3 min, max;
    static AABB from_triangle(const Mesh& mesh, const Triangle& t) {
        Vec3 v0 = mesh.vertices[t.v[0]];
        Vec3 v1 = mesh.vertices[t.v[1]];
        Vec3 v2 = mesh.vertices[t.v[2]];
        return {
            {std::min({v0.x, v1.x, v2.x}), std::min({v0.y, v1.y, v2.y}), std::min({v0.z, v1.z, v2.z})},
            {std::max({v0.x, v1.x, v2.x}), std::max({v0.y, v1.y, v2.y}), std::max({v0.z, v1.z, v2.z})}
        };
    }
    bool intersects(const AABB& o) const {
        return (min.x <= o.max.x && max.x >= o.min.x) &&
               (min.y <= o.max.y && max.y >= o.min.y) &&
               (min.z <= o.max.z && max.z >= o.min.z);
    }
};

struct AABBNode {
    AABB box;
    int triangle_index = -1; // -1 if not leaf
    std::unique_ptr<AABBNode> left, right;
};

std::unique_ptr<AABBNode> build_aabb_tree(const Mesh& mesh, const std::vector<int>& face_indices, int start, int end) {
    auto node = std::make_unique<AABBNode>();
    
    // Calculate AABB for all faces in the current node
    node->box = AABB::from_triangle(mesh, mesh.faces[face_indices[start]]);
    for (int i = start + 1; i < end; ++i) {
        AABB face_box = AABB::from_triangle(mesh, mesh.faces[face_indices[i]]);
        node->box.min = {std::min(node->box.min.x, face_box.min.x), std::min(node->box.min.y, face_box.min.y), std::min(node->box.min.z, face_box.min.z)};
        node->box.max = {std::max(node->box.max.x, face_box.max.x), std::max(node->box.max.y, face_box.max.y), std::max(node->box.max.z, face_box.max.z)};
    }

    if (end - start == 1) {
        node->triangle_index = face_indices[start];
    } else {
        // Split based on the longest axis
        double dx = node->box.max.x - node->box.min.x;
        double dy = node->box.max.y - node->box.min.y;
        double dz = node->box.max.z - node->box.min.z;
        int axis = (dx > dy && dx > dz) ? 0 : (dy > dz ? 1 : 2);

        std::sort(face_indices.begin() + start, face_indices.begin() + end, [&](int a, int b) {
            Vec3 centerA = { (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[0]].x + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[1]].x + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[2]].x) / 3.0,
                             (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[0]].y + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[1]].y + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[2]].y) / 3.0,
                             (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[0]].z + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[1]].z + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[a].v[2]].z) / 3.0 };
            Vec3 centerB = { (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[0]].x + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[1]].x + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[2]].x) / 3.0,
                             (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[0]].y + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[1]].y + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[2]].y) / 3.0,
                             (mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[0]].z + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[1]].z + mesh.vertices[mesh.faces[b].v[2]].z) / 3.0 };
            return (axis == 0 ? centerA.x : (axis == 1 ? centerA.y : centerA.z)) < 
                   (axis == 0 ? centerB.x : (axis == 1 ? centerB.y : centerB.z));
        });

        int mid = start + (end - start) / 2;
        node->left = build_aabb_tree(mesh, const_cast<std::vector<int>&>(face_indices), start, mid);
        node->right = build_aabb_tree(mesh, const_cast<std::vector<int>&>(face_indices), mid, end);
    }
    return node;
}

Mesh read_mesh(int v_count, int f_count) {
    Mesh mesh;
    mesh.vertices.resize(v_count);
    for (int i = 0; i < v_count; ++i) {
        std::cin >> mesh.vertices[i].x >> mesh.vertices[i].y >> mesh.vertices[i].z;
    }
    mesh.faces.resize(f_count);
    for (int i = 0; i < f_count; ++i) {
        std::cin >> mesh.faces[i].v[0] >> mesh.faces[i].v[1] >> mesh.faces[i].v[2];
    }
    return mesh;
}

    std::cout << mesh.vertices.size() << " " << mesh.faces.size() << std::endl;
    for (const auto& v : mesh.vertices) {
        std::cout << v.x << " " << v.y << " " << v.z << std::endl;
    }
    for (const auto& f : mesh.faces) {
        std::cout << f.v[0] << " " << f.v[1] << " " << f.v[2] << std::endl;

}

int main() {
    int va, fa, vb, fb;
    if (!(std::cin >> va >> fa >> vb >> fb)) return 0;

    return 0;
}

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let dims: Vec<usize> = first_line
        .split_whitespace()
        .map(|s| s.parse().unwrap())
        .collect();
    let h = dims[0];
    let w = dims[1];

    let mut grid = Vec::with_capacity(h * w);
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut end = 0;

    for r in 0..h {
        let line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
        for (c, ch) in line.chars().enumerate() {
            if ch == 'A' {
                start = r * w + c;
            } else if ch == 'B' {
                end = r * w + c;
            }
            grid.push(ch as u8);
        }
    }

    let mut parent: Vec<i64> = vec![-1; h * w];
    let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
    queue.push_back(start);
    parent[start] = start as i64;

    let mut found = false;

    while let Some(curr) = queue.pop_front() {
        if curr == end {
            found = true;
            break;
        }

        let r = curr / w;
        let c = curr % w;

        let neighbors = [
            (r as i32 - 1, c as i32),
            (r as i32 + 1, c as i32),
            (r as i32, c as i32 - 1),
            (r as i32, c as i32 + 1),
        ];

        for (nr, nc) in neighbors {
            if nr >= 0 && nr < h as i32 && nc >= 0 && nc < w as i32 {
                let next = nr as usize * w + nc as usize;
                if grid[next] != '#' as u8 && parent[next] == -1 {
                    parent[next] = curr as i64;
                    queue.push_back(next);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if found {
        let mut path = Vec::new();
        let mut curr = end;
        while curr != start {
            path.push(curr);
            curr = parent[curr] as usize;
        }
        path.push(start);
        path.reverse();

        println!("{}", path.len());
        for p in path {
            println!("{} {}", p / w, p % w);
        }
    }
}

Given fixed-length stock material and a shopping list of smaller pieces to cut, use as few stock pieces as possible. Every requested piece must be cut from somewhere, but any leftover material is wasted — so packing the cuts tightly matters.

This is essentially a bin-packing problem and is NP-hard. Subpasses scale from a handful of cuts up to millions, forcing the AI to write code that is both correct and fast. The baseline uses a simple first-fit-decreasing heuristic.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using System.IO;

public class Solution
{
    struct Cut
    {
        public int Index;
        public int Length;
    }

    class Stock
    {
        public int RemainingCapacity;
        public List<int> CutIndices = new List<int>();

        public Stock(int capacity)
        {
            RemainingCapacity = capacity;
        }
    }

    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        string input = Console.In.ReadToEnd();
        string[] tokens = input.Split(new[] { ' ', '\r', '\n', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        if (tokens.Length < 2) return;
        
        int n = int.Parse(tokens[0]);
        int stockLength = int.Parse(tokens[1]);

        Cut[] cuts = new Cut[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        {
            cuts[i] = new Cut { Index = i, Length = int.Parse(tokens[2 + i]) };
        }

        // FFD: Sort cuts descending
        Array.Sort(cuts, (a, b) => b.Length.CompareTo(a.Length));

        List<Stock> stocks = new List<Stock>();

        foreach (var cut in cuts)
        {
            bool placed = false;
            foreach (var stock in stocks)
            {
                if (stock.RemainingCapacity >= cut.Length)
                {
                    stock.RemainingCapacity -= cut.Length;
                    stock.CutIndices.Add(cut.Index);
                    placed = true;
                    break;
                }
            }

            if (!placed)
            {
                Stock newStock = new Stock(stockLength);
                newStock.RemainingCapacity -= cut.Length;
                newStock.CutIndices.Add(cut.Index);
                stocks.Add(newStock);
            }
        }

        Console.WriteLine(stocks.Count);
        foreach (var stock in stocks)
        {
            stock.CutIndices.Sort();
            Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", stock.CutIndices));
        }
    }
}

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

struct Rectangle {
    int id;
    int w, h;
    int x, y;
    bool rotated;
};

struct SkylineSegment {
    int x, y, w;
};

class Bin {
public:
    int width, height;
    std::vector<SkylineSegment> skyline;
    std::vector<Rectangle> packed_items;

    Bin(int w, int h) : width(w), height(h) {
        skyline.push_back({0, 0, w});
    }

    bool add_rect(Rectangle& rect) {
        int best_y = 1e9, best_x = 1e9, best_idx = -1;
        bool best_rotated = false;

        auto try_fit = [&](int w, int h, bool rot) {
            if (w > width || h > height) return;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < skyline.size(); ++i) {
                if (skyline[i].x + w > width) break;
                int max_y = 0, curr_w = 0;
                for (size_t j = i; j < skyline.size(); ++j) {
                    max_y = std::max(max_y, skyline[j].y);
                    curr_w += skyline[j].w;
                    if (curr_w >= w) break;
                }
                if (curr_w >= w && max_y + h <= height) {
                    if (max_y < best_y || (max_y == best_y && skyline[i].x < best_x)) {
                        best_y = max_y;
                        best_x = skyline[i].x;
                        best_idx = i;
                        best_rotated = rot;
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        try_fit(rect.w, rect.h, false);
        try_fit(rect.h, rect.w, true);

        if (best_idx == -1) return false;

        rect.x = best_x;
        rect.y = best_y;
        rect.rotated = best_rotated;
        int rw = best_rotated ? rect.h : rect.w;
        int rh = best_rotated ? rect.w : rect.h;

        std::vector<SkylineSegment> new_skyline;
        for (int i = 0; i < best_idx; ++i) new_skyline.push_back(skyline[i]);
        new_skyline.push_back({best_x, best_y + rh, rw});
        
        int remaining_w = rw;
        size_t j = best_idx;
        while (j < skyline.size() && remaining_w > 0) {
            if (skyline[j].w <= remaining_w) {
                remaining_w -= skyline[j].w;
                j++;
            } else {
                new_skyline.push_back({skyline[j].x + remaining_w, skyline[j].y, skyline[j].w - remaining_w});
                remaining_w = 0;
                j++;
            }
        }
        while (j < skyline.size()) new_skyline.push_back(skyline[j++]);

        skyline.clear();
        for (const auto& s : new_skyline) {
            if (!skyline.empty() && skyline.back().y == s.y) skyline.back().w += s.w;
            else skyline.push_back(s);
        }
        
        packed_items.push_back(rect);
        return true;
    }
};

int main() {
    int N, bin_w, bin_h;
    if (!(std::cin >> N >> bin_w >> bin_h)) return 0;
    std::vector<Rectangle> rects(N);
    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
        rects[i].id = i;
        std::cin >> rects[i].w >> rects[i].h;
    }

    std::sort(rects.begin(), rects.end(), [](const Rectangle& a, const Rectangle& b) {
        return std::max(a.w, a.h) > std::max(b.w, b.h);
    });

    std::vector<Bin> bins;
    for (auto& r : rects) {
        bool packed = false;
        for (int i = std::max(0, (int)bins.size() - 5); i < bins.size(); ++i) {
            if (bins[i].add_rect(r)) {
                packed = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!packed) {
            bins.emplace_back(bin_w, bin_h);
            bins.back().add_rect(r);
        }
    }

    std::cout << bins.size() << "\n";
    std::vector<int> bin_map(N);
    std::vector<int> out_x(N), out_y(N);
    std::vector<bool> out_rot(N);
    for(int i=0; i<bins.size(); ++i) {
        for(const auto& r : bins[i].packed_items) {
            bin_map[r.id] = i + 1;
            out_x[r.id] = r.x;
            out_y[r.id] = r.y;
            out_rot[r.id] = r.rotated;
        }
    }

    for(int i=0; i<N; ++i) {
        std::cout << bin_map[i] << " " << out_x[i] << " " << out_y[i] << " " << (out_rot[i] ? 1 : 0) << "\n";
    }
    
    return 0;
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};
use std::f64::consts::PI;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Polygon {
    vertices: Vec<Point>,
}

// Geometric Utilities
fn is_point_in_polygon(point: &Point, polygon: &Polygon) -> bool {
    let mut inside = false;
    let n = polygon.vertices.len();
    for i in 0..n {
        let j = (i + 1) % n;
        let vi = &polygon.vertices[i];
        let vj = &polygon.vertices[j];
        if ((vi.y > point.y) != (vj.y > point.y)) &&
           (point.x < (vj.x - vi.x) * (point.y - vi.y) / (vj.y - vi.y) + vi.x) {
            inside = !inside;
        }
    }
    inside
}

fn is_polygon_in_polygon(inner: &Polygon, outer: &Polygon) -> bool {
    for vertex in &inner.vertices {
        if !is_point_in_polygon(vertex, outer) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    true
}

// Simple SAT-based intersection check (axis-aligned bounding box or simplified separating axis theorem would be better)
// Using a simple point-in-polygon check is insufficient for full intersection, 
// but for a greedy prototype it might suffice if checking all vertices.
fn polygons_overlap(poly1: &Polygon, poly2: &Polygon) -> bool {
    // Check if any point of poly1 is inside poly2
    for p in &poly1.vertices {
        if is_point_in_polygon(p, poly2) { return true; }
    }
    // Check if any point of poly2 is inside poly1
    for p in &poly2.vertices {
        if is_point_in_polygon(p, poly1) { return true; }
    }
    false
}

fn rotate_point(p: Point, angle: f64) -> Point {
    let s = angle.sin();
    let c = angle.cos();
    Point {
        x: p.x * c - p.y * s,
        y: p.x * s + p.y * c,
    }
}

fn transform_polygon(poly: &Polygon, translation: Point, rotation: f64) -> Polygon {
    let new_vertices = poly.vertices.iter()
        .map(|&p| {
            let rotated = rotate_point(p, rotation);
            Point { x: rotated.x + translation.x, y: rotated.y + translation.y }
        })
        .collect();
    Polygon { vertices: new_vertices }
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
        let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
        if parts.len() == 2 {
            let sv: usize = parts[0].parse().expect("Invalid SV");
            let np: usize = parts[1].parse().expect("Invalid NP");

            let mut stock_vertices = Vec::with_capacity(sv);
            for _ in 0..sv {
                if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
                    let p: Vec<f64> = line.split_whitespace()
                        .map(|s| s.parse().expect("Invalid point coordinate"))
                        .collect();
                    stock_vertices.push(Point { x: p[0], y: p[1] });
                }
            }
            let stock = Polygon { vertices: stock_vertices };
            
            let mut pieces = Vec::with_capacity(np);
            for _ in 0..np {
                if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
                    let pv: usize = line.trim().parse().expect("Invalid PV");
                    let mut piece_vertices = Vec::with_capacity(pv);
                    for _ in 0..pv {
                        if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
                            let p: Vec<f64> = line.split_whitespace()
                                .map(|s| s.parse().expect("Invalid point coordinate"))
                                .collect();
                            piece_vertices.push(Point { x: p[0], y: p[1] });
                        }
                    }
                    pieces.push(Polygon { vertices: piece_vertices });
                }
            }
            
            // Packing Logic: Greedy placement
            let mut placed_polygons = Vec::new();
            let mut placements = Vec::new();
            
            for piece in pieces {
                let mut found = false;
                // Try basic grid of translations and rotations
                'search: for rot in (0..4).map(|i| i as f64 * PI / 2.0) {
                    for x in (0..10).map(|i| i as f64 * 1.0) {
                        for y in (0..10).map(|i| i as f64 * 1.0) {
                            let candidate = transform_polygon(&piece, Point { x, y }, rot);
                            if is_polygon_in_polygon(&candidate, &stock) {
                                let mut overlap = false;
                                for p in &placed_polygons {
                                    if polygons_overlap(&candidate, p) {
                                        overlap = true;
                                        break;
                                    }
                                }
                                if !overlap {
                                    placements.push((0, x, y, rot));
                                    placed_polygons.push(candidate);
                                    found = true;
                                    break 'search;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            
            // Output
            println!("1"); 
            for placement in placements {
                println!("{} {} {} {}", placement.0, placement.1, placement.2, placement.3);
            }
        }
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Numerics;

namespace BinPacking3D
{
    // Basic representation of a 3D vertex
    public record Vertex(double X, double Y, double Z);

    // Basic representation of a 3D face (indices into vertex list)
    public record Face(int A, int B, int C);

    // Representation of a Polyhedron
    public class Polyhedron
    {
        public List<Vertex> Vertices { get; } = new();
        public List<Face> Faces { get; } = new();
        public Vector3 Min { get; private set; }
        public Vector3 Max { get; private set; }

        public Polyhedron(List<Vertex> vertices, List<Face> faces)
        {
            Vertices = vertices;
            Faces = faces;
            CalculateAABB();
        }

        private void CalculateAABB()
        {
            float minX = float.MaxValue, minY = float.MaxValue, minZ = float.MaxValue;
            float maxX = float.MinValue, maxY = float.MinValue, maxZ = float.MinValue;
            foreach (var v in Vertices)
            {
                minX = Math.Min(minX, (float)v.X);
                minY = Math.Min(minY, (float)v.Y);
                minZ = Math.Min(minZ, (float)v.Z);
                maxX = Math.Max(maxX, (float)v.X);
                maxY = Math.Max(maxY, (float)v.Y);
                maxZ = Math.Max(maxZ, (float)v.Z);
            }
            Min = new Vector3(minX, minY, minZ);
            Max = new Vector3(maxX, maxY, maxZ);
        }

        public Vector3 Size => Max - Min;
    }

    public record Placement(Vector3 Translation, Quaternion Rotation);

    // Solver class to hold the logic
    public class Solver
    {
        public void Solve()
        {
            var (polyhedron, containerDims) = ReadInput();
            
            var placements = new List<Placement>();
            var placedItems = new List<(Placement, Polyhedron)>();

            // Greedy grid-based packing
            float stepX = polyhedron.Size.X;
            float stepY = polyhedron.Size.Y;
            float stepZ = polyhedron.Size.Z;

            for (float x = 0; x + polyhedron.Size.X <= containerDims.X; x += stepX)
            {
                for (float y = 0; y + polyhedron.Size.Y <= containerDims.Y; y += stepY)
                {
                    for (float z = 0; z + polyhedron.Size.Z <= containerDims.Z; z += stepZ)
                    {
                        var pos = new Vector3(x, y, z);
                        var p = new Placement(pos, Quaternion.Identity);
                        
                        // Check collision with already placed items
                        bool collision = false;
                        foreach (var (existingP, existingPoly) in placedItems)
                        {
                            // Basic AABB overlap check
                            var min1 = existingP.Translation + existingPoly.Min;
                            var max1 = existingP.Translation + existingPoly.Max;
                            var min2 = p.Translation + polyhedron.Min;
                            var max2 = p.Translation + polyhedron.Max;

                            if (min1.X < max2.X && max1.X > min2.X &&
                                min1.Y < max2.Y && max1.Y > min2.Y &&
                                min1.Z < max2.Z && max1.Z > min2.Z)
                            {
                                collision = true;
                                break;
                            }
                        }

                        if (!collision)
                        {
                            placements.Add(p);
                            placedItems.Add((p, polyhedron));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            // Print output
            Console.WriteLine(placements.Count);
            foreach (var p in placements)
            {
                Console.WriteLine($"{p.Translation.X} {p.Translation.Y} {p.Translation.Z} {p.Rotation.W} {p.Rotation.X} {p.Rotation.Y} {p.Rotation.Z}");
            }
        }

        private (Polyhedron, Vector3) ReadInput()
        {
            // Keeping the implementation from previous turn
            string[] line1 = Console.ReadLine()!.Split();
            int V = int.Parse(line1[0]);
            int F = int.Parse(line1[1]);

            var vertices = new List<Vertex>();
            for (int i = 0; i < V; i++)
            {
                string[] v = Console.ReadLine()!.Split();
                vertices.Add(new Vertex(double.Parse(v[0]), double.Parse(v[1]), double.Parse(v[2])));
            }

            var faces = new List<Face>();
            for (int i = 0; i < F; i++)
            {
                string[] f = Console.ReadLine()!.Split();
                faces.Add(new Face(int.Parse(f[0]), int.Parse(f[1]), int.Parse(f[2])));
            }

            string[] container = Console.ReadLine()!.Split();
            var containerDims = new Vector3((float)double.Parse(container[0]), (float)double.Parse(container[1]), (float)double.Parse(container[2]));

            return (new Polyhedron(vertices, faces), containerDims);
        }
    }

    class Program
    {
        static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            new Solver().Solve();
        }
    }
}

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
#include <deque>

// Suffix Array construction using O(N log N) prefix doubling
struct SuffixArray {
    std::vector<int> sa, lcp, rank;
    std::vector<int> s;
    int n;

    SuffixArray(const std::vector<int>& input, int max_val) : s(input), n(input.size()) {
        sa.resize(n);
        rank.resize(n);
        std::vector<int> tmp(n);

        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            sa[i] = i;
            rank[i] = s[i];
        }

        for (int k = 1; k < n; k <<= 1) {
            auto cmp = [&](int i, int j) {
                if (rank[i] != rank[j]) return rank[i] < rank[j];
                int ri = (i + k < n) ? rank[i + k] : -1;
                int rj = (j + k < n) ? rank[j + k] : -1;
                return ri < rj;
            };
            std::sort(sa.begin(), sa.end(), cmp);
            tmp[sa[0]] = 0;
            for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
                tmp[sa[i]] = tmp[sa[i - 1]] + (cmp(sa[i - 1], sa[i]) ? 1 : 0);
            }
            rank = tmp;
            if (rank[sa[n - 1]] == n - 1) break;
        }

        // Kasai's algorithm for LCP
        lcp.assign(n, 0);
        int h = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            if (rank[i] > 0) {
                int j = sa[rank[i] - 1];
                if (h > 0) h--;
                while (i + h < n && j + h < n && s[i + h] == s[j + h]) h++;
                lcp[rank[i]] = h;
            }
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n;
    if (!(std::cin >> n)) return 0;
    if (n == 0) return 0;

    std::vector<std::string> strings(n);
    std::vector<int> combined;
    std::vector<int> owner;
    int sentinel = -1;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        std::cin >> strings[i];
        for (char c : strings[i]) {
            combined.push_back((unsigned char)c + 256); // Offset to avoid conflict with sentinels
            owner.push_back(i);
        }
        combined.push_back(sentinel--);
        owner.push_back(-1);
    }

    if (n == 1) {
        std::cout << strings[0] << std::endl;
        return 0;
    }

    SuffixArray sa_obj(combined, 256 + 256);
    
    // Sliding window to find LCS
    int left = 0;
    std::vector<int> count(n, 0);
    int distinct = 0;
    int max_len = 0;
    int best_pos = -1;

    // dq stores indices of LCP array such that lcp[dq] is monotonic increasing
    std::deque<int> dq; 

    for (int right = 0; right < combined.size(); ++right) {
        if (owner[sa_obj.sa[right]] != -1) {
            if (count[owner[sa_obj.sa[right]]]++ == 0) distinct++;
        }
        
        // When adding new element to right, LCP[right] is the candidate
        if (right > 0) {
            while (!dq.empty() && sa_obj.lcp[dq.back()] >= sa_obj.lcp[right]) dq.pop_back();
            dq.push_back(right);
        }

        while (distinct == n) {
            // Window is [left, right]
            // Valid LCP range for this window is [left+1, right]
            while (!dq.empty() && dq.front() <= left) dq.pop_front();
            
            if (!dq.empty()) {
                int current_min_lcp = sa_obj.lcp[dq.front()];
                if (current_min_lcp > max_len) {
                    max_len = current_min_lcp;
                    best_pos = sa_obj.sa[right];
                }
            }
            
            if (owner[sa_obj.sa[left]] != -1) {
                if (--count[owner[sa_obj.sa[left]]] == 0) distinct--;
            }
            left++;
        }
    }

    if (best_pos != -1) {
        for (int i = 0; i < max_len; ++i) {
            std::cout << (char)(combined[best_pos + i] - 256);
        }
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}

using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

namespace MinesweeperSolver
{
    public class Solver
    {
        private readonly Board _board;

        public Solver(Board board)
        {
            _board = board;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Performs a single pass of the solver, applying basic deduction rules
        /// to identify mines and safe cells.
        /// </summary>
        public void SolveStep()
        {
            // The solver iteratively applies two fundamental Minesweeper rules:
            // 1. If the number of hidden neighbors equals the neighbor mine count, all hidden neighbors are mines.
            // 2. If the number of flagged neighbors equals the neighbor mine count, all other hidden neighbors are safe.

            bool madeProgress = true;
            while (madeProgress)
            {
                madeProgress = false;
                foreach (var cell in GetAllCells())
                {
                    // Only apply logic to revealed cells that have a known neighbor mine count.
                    if (cell.State != CellState.Revealed || !cell.NeighborMineCount.HasValue)
                        continue;

                    var neighbors = _board.GetNeighbors(cell).ToList();
                    var hiddenNeighbors = neighbors.Where(n => n.State == CellState.Hidden).ToList();
                    var flaggedNeighbors = neighbors.Where(n => n.State == CellState.Flagged).ToList();

                    if (hiddenNeighbors.Count == 0) continue;

                    // Rule 1: Identify mines
                    // If the number of hidden neighbors + already flagged neighbors equals the total mine count, 
                    // then all remaining hidden neighbors MUST be mines.
                    if (cell.NeighborMineCount == flaggedNeighbors.Count + hiddenNeighbors.Count)
                    {
                        foreach (var hidden in hiddenNeighbors)
                        {
                            hidden.State = CellState.Flagged;
                            hidden.IsMine = true;
                            madeProgress = true;
                        }
                    }
                    // Rule 2: Identify safe cells
                    // If the number of flagged neighbors equals the total mine count,
                    // then all remaining hidden neighbors MUST be safe.
                    else if (cell.NeighborMineCount == flaggedNeighbors.Count)
                    {
                        foreach (var hidden in hiddenNeighbors)
                        {
                            // This would be the 'Reveal' action in a real game
                            hidden.State = CellState.Revealed;
                            madeProgress = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        private IEnumerable<Cell> GetAllCells()
        {
            for (int x = 0; x < _board.Width; x++)
            {
                for (int y = 0; y < _board.Height; y++)
                {
                    yield return _board.GetCell(x, y);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Vec3 {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Quat {
    w: f64,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
}

struct Tetrahedron {
    pos: Vec3,
    rot: Quat,
    scale: f64,
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let nv: usize = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap().trim().parse().unwrap();
    let mut vertices = Vec::with_capacity(nv);
    for _ in 0..nv {
        let line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
        let coords: Vec<f64> = line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
        vertices.push(Vec3 { x: coords[0], y: coords[1], z: 0.0 });
    }

    let sun_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let sun: Vec<f64> = sun_line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.parse().unwrap()).collect();
    let _sun_dir = Vec3 { x: sun[0], y: sun[1], z: sun[2] };

    // Simple strategy: cover the polygon with a grid of tetrahedrons
    // For a real solution, we would need a more sophisticated covering algorithm.
    // This is a placeholder to demonstrate the output format.
    let mut tetrahedrons = Vec::new();
    tetrahedrons.push(Tetrahedron {
        pos: Vec3 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 },
        rot: Quat { w: 1.0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 },
        scale: 1.0,
    });

    println!("{}", tetrahedrons.len());
    for t in tetrahedrons {
        println!("{:.6} {:.6} {:.6} {:.6} {:.6} {:.6} {:.6} {:.6}", 
            t.pos.x, t.pos.y, t.pos.z, 
            t.rot.w, t.rot.x, t.rot.y, t.rot.z, 
            t.scale);
    }
}

Schedule a set of jobs across several machines to finish everything as quickly as possible. Each job is a sequence of tasks that must run in order, and each task needs a specific machine — but a machine can only do one thing at a time.

This classic factory-scheduling problem is NP-hard. Subpasses increase the number of jobs and machines. The baseline greedily starts whichever task can begin earliest.

Job-Shop Scheduling - 3 jobs, 2 machines

View Code (2787 chars)
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <queue>
#include <algorithm>

struct Task {
    int id;
    int machine;
    int duration;
    int start_time;
    int end_time;
};

struct Job {
    int id;
    std::vector<Task> tasks;
    int next_task_idx = 0;
};

// Simple greedy scheduling logic
void solve() {
    int num_jobs, num_machines;
    if (!(std::cin >> num_jobs >> num_machines)) return;

    std::vector<Job> jobs(num_jobs);
    for (int i = 0; i < num_jobs; ++i) {
        jobs[i].id = i;
        int num_tasks;
        std::cin >> num_tasks;
        for (int j = 0; j < num_tasks; ++j) {
            int m, d;
            std::cin >> m >> d;
            jobs[i].tasks.push_back({j, m, d, -1, -1});
        }
    }

    std::vector<int> machine_free_time(num_machines, 0);
    std::vector<int> job_next_available_time(num_jobs, 0);

    // Using a priority queue or simple loop to schedule tasks.
    // Given the "extreme" scale requirement, a simple greedy approach:
    // Always pick the next available task for each job that can start earliest.
    
    // For simplicity and speed in this version, iterate until all tasks scheduled.
    int tasks_scheduled = 0;
    int total_tasks = 0;
    for(const auto& job : jobs) total_tasks += job.tasks.size();

    while (tasks_scheduled < total_tasks) {
        int best_job_idx = -1;
        int earliest_start = 2e9;

        for (int i = 0; i < num_jobs; ++i) {
            if (jobs[i].next_task_idx < jobs[i].tasks.size()) {
                Task& t = jobs[i].tasks[jobs[i].next_task_idx];
                int machine_ready = machine_free_time[t.machine];
                int job_ready = job_next_available_time[i];
                int start = std::max(machine_ready, job_ready);
                
                if (start < earliest_start) {
                    earliest_start = start;
                    best_job_idx = i;
                }
            }
        }

        if (best_job_idx != -1) {
            Task& t = jobs[best_job_idx].tasks[jobs[best_job_idx].next_task_idx];
            t.start_time = earliest_start;
            t.end_time = t.start_time + t.duration;
            machine_free_time[t.machine] = t.end_time;
            job_next_available_time[best_job_idx] = t.end_time;
            jobs[best_job_idx].next_task_idx++;
            tasks_scheduled++;
        }
    }

    // Output
    for (int i = 0; i < num_jobs; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < jobs[i].tasks.size(); ++j) {
            std::cout << jobs[i].tasks[j].start_time << " " << jobs[i].tasks[j].machine;
            if (j < jobs[i].tasks.size() - 1) std::cout << " ";
        }
        std::cout << std::endl;
    }
}

int main() {
    std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(NULL);
    solve();
    return 0;
}

This 3D packing problem is NP-hard. Subpasses increase the number and variety of box sizes. The baseline uses a greedy first-fit approach.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

public struct Box
{
    public int Id;
    public int W, H, D;
    public int X, Y, Z;
}

public struct Space
{
    public int X, Y, Z, W, H, D;
}

public class Packer
{
    private int containerW, containerH, containerD;
    private List<Space> freeSpaces = new List<Space>();
    private List<Box> packedBoxes = new List<Box>();

    public Packer(int w, int h, int d)
    {
        containerW = w;
        containerH = h;
        containerD = d;
        freeSpaces.Add(new Space { X = 0, Y = 0, Z = 0, W = w, H = h, D = d });
    }

    public void Pack(List<Box> boxes)
    {
        // Sort by volume descending
        var sortedBoxes = boxes.OrderByDescending(b => (long)b.W * b.H * b.D).ToList();

        foreach (var box in sortedBoxes)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < freeSpaces.Count; i++)
            {
                var space = freeSpaces[i];
                if (box.W <= space.W && box.H <= space.H && box.D <= space.D)
                {
                    // Place box
                    var placedBox = new Box
                    {
                        Id = box.Id,
                        W = box.W, H = box.H, D = box.D,
                        X = space.X, Y = space.Y, Z = space.Z
                    };
                    packedBoxes.Add(placedBox);

                    // Split space
                    freeSpaces.RemoveAt(i);
                    SplitSpace(space, placedBox);
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private void SplitSpace(Space space, Box box)
    {
        // Simple split into 3 new spaces
        if (space.W > box.W)
            freeSpaces.Add(new Space { X = space.X + box.W, Y = space.Y, Z = space.Z, W = space.W - box.W, H = box.H, D = box.D });
        if (space.H > box.H)
            freeSpaces.Add(new Space { X = space.X, Y = space.Y + box.H, Z = space.Z, W = space.W, H = space.H - box.H, D = box.D });
        if (space.D > box.D)
            freeSpaces.Add(new Space { X = space.X, Y = space.Y, Z = space.Z + box.D, W = space.W, H = space.H, D = space.D - box.D });
    }

    public void PrintResult()
    {
        Console.WriteLine(packedBoxes.Count);
        foreach (var b in packedBoxes)
        {
            Console.WriteLine(string.Format("{0} {1} {2} {3}", b.Id, b.X, b.Y, b.Z));
        }
    }
}

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        string line = Console.ReadLine();
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(line)) return;
        var parts = line.Split(' ');
        int n = int.Parse(parts[0]);
        int w = int.Parse(parts[1]);
        int h = int.Parse(parts[2]);
        int d = int.Parse(parts[3]);

        var boxes = new List<Box>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        {
            var dims = Console.ReadLine().Split(' ').Select(int.Parse).ToArray();
            boxes.Add(new Box { Id = i, W = dims[0], H = dims[1], D = dims[2] });
        }

        var packer = new Packer(w, h, d);
        packer.Pack(boxes);
        packer.PrintResult();
    }
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing a C# program to solve a mining problem in a simplified 3D voxel space.

**Constraints:**
1. Can only dig dirt that is exposed from above or a side.
2. Dug dirt must be dumped somewhere - at a location not blocking future digging
3. Maximum uphill slope - 1 Z voxel per X/Y voxel.
4. Dumped dirt becomes a new obstacle (plan carefully!)
5. Goal is to get valuable ore to a processing plant located at x=0, y=0
6. Ground is stable and solid, and you can dig under any voxel without fear of it collapsing
so long as it's connected to the earth. If you disconnect a voxel(s), it will collapse.

The voxel grid size has 10x more precision in Z than X/Y. So 10x10x100 is a cube.

**Input header format (stdin - space delimited. Ends with newline):**
```
XVoxelCount YVoxelCount ZVoxelCount XBlockSize YBlockSize ZBlockSize
```
Counts are human readable integers. BlockSize are human readable decimal numbers.

After the newline, voxels then follow in bytes, like this python psuedocode:
```
for x in range(XVoxelCount):
for y in range(YVoxelCount):
for z in range(ZVoxelCount):
d = readByte(stdin)
massInTonnes = d % 16
valuePerTonne = d // 16
addVoxel(d)
```

Each peice of dirt needs to be moved to its new location - you need to trace the
path in X and Y (4-connected / manhatten steps) and ensure that the path doesn't climb uphill
or downhill more than 1 Z voxel for every X/Y voxel.

**Output format (stdout / newline seperated):**
```
M (number of operations)
N digX digY digZ stepX1 stepY1 stepX2 stepY2 (N steps) destX destY (for each operation)
```

If dumping valuable ore at the processing plant, the voxel ceases to exist. If a voxel is
dumped elsewhere, it is dumped on top of the ground, raising the ground by 1 voxel. It can
be dug again and moved later if required.

Every unit of mass requires $1 of fuel to move one voxel in X or Y when flat, or $5 of fuel
to go up a 10% slope. Downhill is free.

Getting valuable ore to your processing plant pays $1000 per unit of mass per unit of value.
The most valuable ore (#15) pays $15,000 per ton, so the most a single dump truck load can gross
is $225,000.

(Dumping junk ore at the processing plant causes damage to the plant, costing $1000 per ton.)

1. Program must compile with .NET/csc
2. Read from stdin, write to stdout
3. World size could be anything from 10x10x10 to 5000x5000x5000, your code should handle both extremes.
4. Your code should complete in under 5 minutes
5. Maximize profit.

use std::io::{self, BufRead};

struct Sample {
    depth: f64,
    measurements: Vec<f64>,
}

struct Drillhole {
    id: String,
    start: [f64; 3],
    direction: [f64; 3],
    _length: f64,
    samples: Vec<Sample>,
}

struct Suspect {
    hole_id: String,
    sample_idx: usize,
    property_idx: usize,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let parts: Vec<&str> = first_line.split_whitespace().collect();
    let num_holes: usize = parts[0].parse().unwrap();
    let num_properties: usize = parts[1].parse().unwrap();

    let property_names: Vec<String> = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap()
        .split_whitespace().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();

    let mut drillholes = Vec::with_capacity(num_holes);

    for _ in 0..num_holes {
        let hole_info = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
        let h: Vec<&str> = hole_info.split_whitespace().collect();
        let id = h[0].to_string();
        let start = [h[1].parse().unwrap(), h[2].parse().unwrap(), h[3].parse().unwrap()];
        let direction = [h[4].parse().unwrap(), h[5].parse().unwrap(), h[6].parse().unwrap()];
        let _length = h[7].parse().unwrap();
        let num_samples: usize = h[8].parse().unwrap();

        let mut samples = Vec::with_capacity(num_samples);
        for _ in 0..num_samples {
            let sample_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
            let s: Vec<&str> = sample_line.split_whitespace().collect();
            let depth = s[0].parse().unwrap();
            let measurements: Vec<f64> = s[1..].iter().map(|&x| x.parse().unwrap()).collect();
            samples.push(Sample { depth, measurements });
        }

        drillholes.push(Drillhole { id, start, direction, _length, samples });
    }

    let suspects = detect_outliers(&drillholes, num_properties);
    
    println!("{}", suspects.len());
    for s in suspects {
        println!("{} {} {} {:.4}", s.hole_id, s.sample_idx, property_names[s.property_idx], s.confidence);
    }
}

fn detect_outliers(drillholes: &[Drillhole], num_properties: usize) -> Vec<Suspect> {
    let mut suspects = Vec::new();
    
    // Calculate global statistics for each property
    let mut sums = vec![0.0; num_properties];
    let mut counts = vec![0.0; num_properties];
    
    for hole in drillholes {
        for sample in &hole.samples {
            for (i, &val) in sample.measurements.iter().enumerate() {
                sums[i] += val;
                counts[i] += 1.0;
            }
        }
    }
    
    let means: Vec<f64> = sums.iter().zip(counts.iter()).map(|(&s, &c)| s / c).collect();
    
    // Identify suspects as those significantly deviating from the mean (e.g., > 3 std devs)
    // Note: A more robust approach would use spatial neighbors, but Z-score is a good start.
    
    for (h_idx, hole) in drillholes.iter().enumerate() {
        for (s_idx, sample) in hole.samples.iter().enumerate() {
            for (p_idx, &val) in sample.measurements.iter().enumerate() {
                let diff = (val - means[p_idx]).abs();
                if diff > 10.0 { // Arbitrary threshold for "obvious" outlier
                    suspects.push(Suspect {
                        hole_id: hole.id.clone(),
                        sample_idx: s_idx,
                        property_idx: p_idx,
                        confidence: diff / 10.0, // Simplistic confidence
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    suspects.sort_by(|a, b| b.confidence.partial_cmp(&a.confidence).unwrap());
    suspects
}

- **Large**: 6D-8D games (eg 4x4x4x4x4x4 to 6x6x6x6x6x6x6x6), many obstacles, complex pathfinding

**The Challenge:**
Your C++ snake player will be tested with games ranging from simple 2D boards to massive 20D hypercubes.
The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL dimensionalities.

**Problem:**
Like classic Nokia snake, but generalized to arbitrary dimensions. The snake occupies a series of
connected integer grid points in N-D space, moves one step per turn along one axis (+1 or -1),
grows when eating food, and dies if it hits an obstacle or itself.

**Input format (stdin, whitespace / newline seperated):**

**Output format (stdout):**

- axis: 0 to D-1 (which dimension to move along)
- direction: -1 or +1 (which way to move)

**Game ends when:**
- Snake eats all food (win)
- Snake hits obstacle or itself (lose)
- Max turns reached

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <deque>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <queue>

struct Point {
    std::vector<int> coords;

    bool operator==(const Point& other) const {
        return coords == other.coords;
    }
};

struct PointHash {
    std::size_t operator()(const Point& p) const {
        std::size_t seed = 0;
        for (int x : p.coords) {
            seed ^= std::hash<int>{}(x) + 0x9e3779b9 + (seed << 6) + (seed >> 2);
        }
        return seed;
    }
};

class SnakeGame {
public:
    int D;
    int max_turns;
    std::vector<int> bounds;
    std::deque<Point> snake;
    std::unordered_set<Point, PointHash> food;
    std::unordered_set<Point, PointHash> obstacles;

    int manhattan_distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {
        int dist = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) dist += std::abs(p1.coords[i] - p2.coords[i]);
        return dist;
    }

    bool is_valid(const Point& p) {
        for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
            if (p.coords[i] < 0 || p.coords[i] >= bounds[i]) return false;
        }
        if (obstacles.count(p)) return false;
        for (const auto& segment : snake) {
            if (p == segment) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    void run() {
        for (int turn = 0; turn < max_turns; ++turn) {
            if (food.empty()) break;

            // Simple greedy approach: find closest food
            Point target = *food.begin();
            int min_dist = 1e9;
            for (const auto& f : food) {
                int d = manhattan_distance(snake.front(), f);
                if (d < min_dist) {
                    min_dist = d;
                    target = f;
                }
            }

            // Find next move
            Point head = snake.front();
            for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
                for (int dir : {-1, 1}) {
                    Point next = head;
                    next.coords[i] += dir;
                    if (is_valid(next)) {
                        std::cout << i << " " << dir << std::endl;
                        // Move snake
                        snake.push_front(next);
                        if (food.count(next)) {
                            food.erase(next);
                        } else {
                            snake.pop_back();
                        }
                        goto next_turn;
                    }
                }
            }
            break; // No move found
            next_turn:;
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    int D, max_turns;
    if (!(std::cin >> D >> max_turns)) return 0;

    SnakeGame game;
    game.D = D;
    game.max_turns = max_turns;
    game.bounds.resize(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) std::cin >> game.bounds[i];

    int snake_length;
    std::cin >> snake_length;
    Point head;
    head.coords.resize(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) std::cin >> head.coords[i];
    game.snake.push_back(head);
    // Note: Assuming initial snake length is 1 for now, or need to handle body construction

    int F;
    std::cin >> F;
    for (int i = 0; i < F; ++i) {
        Point p;
        p.coords.resize(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) std::cin >> p.coords[j];
        game.food.insert(p);
    }

    int O;
    std::cin >> O;
    for (int i = 0; i < O; ++i) {
        Point p;
        p.coords.resize(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) std::cin >> p.coords[j];
        game.obstacles.insert(p);
    }

    game.run();
    return 0;
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

public class TetrisAI
{
    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        string inputLine = Console.ReadLine();
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(inputLine)) return;
        string[] input = inputLine.Split(new char[] { ' ' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int width = int.Parse(input[0]);
        int height = int.Parse(input[1]);
        int numPieces = int.Parse(input[2]);

        Board board = new Board(width, height);

        for (int i = 0; i < numPieces; i++)
        {
            string pieceType = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            
            var bestMove = board.GetBestMove(pieceType);
            Console.WriteLine(string.Format("{0} {1}", bestMove.Rotation, bestMove.Column));
            
            string result = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            board.ApplyMove(pieceType, bestMove);
        }
    }
}

    public int Rotation { get; set; }
    public int Column { get; set; }
    public double Score { get; set; }
}

public class Board
{
    private int width;
    private int height;
    private int[,] grid;

    public Board(int width, int height)
    {
        this.width = width;
        this.height = height;
        this.grid = new int[height, width];
    }

    public Move GetBestMove(string pieceType)
    {
        Move bestMove = new Move { Score = double.MinValue };
        var rotations = PieceDefinitions.Pieces[pieceType];

        for (int r = 0; r < rotations.Count; r++)
        {
            var rotation = rotations[r];
            for (int col = 0; col <= width - GetPieceWidth(rotation); col++)
            {
                var simulatedGrid = SimulatePlacement(rotation, col);
                if (simulatedGrid != null)
                {
                    double score = CalculateScore(simulatedGrid);
                    if (score > bestMove.Score)
                    {
                        bestMove = new Move { Rotation = r, Column = col, Score = score };
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return bestMove;
    }

    private int GetPieceWidth(int[,] rotation)
    {
        int maxCol = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
            if (rotation[i, 1] > maxCol) maxCol = rotation[i, 1];
        return maxCol + 1;
    }

    private int[,] SimulatePlacement(int[,] rotation, int col)
    {
        int[,] newGrid = (int[,])grid.Clone();
        for (int row = 0; row < height; row++)
        {
            if (CanPlace(newGrid, rotation, row, col))
            {
                if (!CanPlace(newGrid, rotation, row + 1, col))
                {
                    Place(newGrid, rotation, row, col);
                    ClearLines(newGrid);
                    return newGrid;
                }
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private bool CanPlace(int[,] grid, int[,] rotation, int row, int col)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
        {
            int r = row + rotation[i, 0];
            int c = col + rotation[i, 1];
            if (r >= height || c < 0 || c >= width || (r >= 0 && grid[r, c] == 1))
                return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    private void Place(int[,] grid, int[,] rotation, int row, int col)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
        {
            int r = row + rotation[i, 0];
            int c = col + rotation[i, 1];
            if (r >= 0) grid[r, c] = 1;
        }
    }

    private int ClearLines(int[,] grid)
    {
        int cleared = 0;
        for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                if (grid[r, c] == 0) full = false;
            if (full)
            {
                cleared++;
                for (int i = r; i > 0; i--)
                    for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                        grid[i, c] = grid[i - 1, c];
                for (int c = 0; c < width; c++) grid[0, c] = 0;
                r++; 
            }
        }
        return cleared;
    }

    private double CalculateScore(int[,] grid)
    {
        int aggregateHeight = 0;
        int holes = 0;
        int bumpiness = 0;

        int[] columnHeights = new int[width];
        for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
        {
            for (int r = 0; r < height; r++)
            {
                if (grid[r, c] == 1)
                {
                    columnHeights[c] = height - r;
                    break;
                }
            }
            aggregateHeight += columnHeights[c];
        }

        for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
        {
            if (c < width - 1)
                bumpiness += Math.Abs(columnHeights[c] - columnHeights[c + 1]);

            for (int r = height - columnHeights[c]; r < height; r++)
            {
                if (grid[r, c] == 0) holes++;
            }
        }

        return -(aggregateHeight * 0.51) - (holes * 0.35) - (bumpiness * 0.18);
    }

    public void ApplyMove(string pieceType, Move move)
    {
        var rotation = PieceDefinitions.Pieces[pieceType][move.Rotation];
        // For actual placement, we need to find the correct row
        int row = 0;
        while (CanPlace(grid, rotation, row + 1, move.Column)) row++;
        Place(grid, rotation, row, move.Column);
        ClearLines(grid);
    }
}

public class Board
{
    private int width;
    private int height;
    private int[,] grid;

    public Board(int width, int height)
    {
        this.width = width;
        this.height = height;
        this.grid = new int[height, width];
    }

    public Move GetBestMove(string pieceType)
    {
        Move bestMove = new Move { Score = double.MinValue };
        var rotations = PieceDefinitions.Pieces[pieceType];

        for (int r = 0; r < rotations.Count; r++)
        {
            var rotation = rotations[r];
            for (int col = 0; col <= width - GetPieceWidth(rotation); col++)
            {
                var simulatedGrid = SimulatePlacement(rotation, col);
                if (simulatedGrid != null)
                {
                    double score = CalculateScore(simulatedGrid);
                    if (score > bestMove.Score)
                    {
                        bestMove = new Move { Rotation = r, Column = col, Score = score };
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return bestMove;
    }

    private int GetPieceWidth(int[,] rotation)
    {
        int maxCol = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
            if (rotation[i, 1] > maxCol) maxCol = rotation[i, 1];
        return maxCol + 1;
    }

    private int[,] SimulatePlacement(int[,] rotation, int col)
    {
        int[,] newGrid = (int[,])grid.Clone();
        for (int row = 0; row < height; row++)
        {
            if (CanPlace(newGrid, rotation, row, col))
            {
                if (!CanPlace(newGrid, rotation, row + 1, col))
                {
                    Place(newGrid, rotation, row, col);
                    ClearLines(newGrid);
                    return newGrid;
                }
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private bool CanPlace(int[,] grid, int[,] rotation, int row, int col)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
        {
            int r = row + rotation[i, 0];
            int c = col + rotation[i, 1];
            if (r >= height || c < 0 || c >= width || (r >= 0 && grid[r, c] == 1))
                return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    private void Place(int[,] grid, int[,] rotation, int row, int col)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < rotation.GetLength(0); i++)
        {
            int r = row + rotation[i, 0];
            int c = col + rotation[i, 1];
            if (r >= 0) grid[r, c] = 1;
        }
    }

    private int ClearLines(int[,] grid)
    {
        int cleared = 0;
        for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                if (grid[r, c] == 0) full = false;
            if (full)
            {
                cleared++;
                for (int i = r; i > 0; i--)
                    for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                        grid[i, c] = grid[i - 1, c];
                for (int c = 0; c < width; c++) grid[0, c] = 0;
                r++; 
            }
        }
        return cleared;
    }

    private double CalculateScore(int[,] grid)
    {
        int aggregateHeight = 0;
        int holes = 0;
        int bumpiness = 0;

        int[] columnHeights = new int[width];
        for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
        {
            for (int r = 0; r < height; r++)
            {
                if (grid[r, c] == 1)
                {
                    columnHeights[c] = height - r;
                    break;
                }
            }
            aggregateHeight += columnHeights[c];
        }

        for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
        {
            if (c < width - 1)
                bumpiness += Math.Abs(columnHeights[c] - columnHeights[c + 1]);

            for (int r = height - columnHeights[c]; r < height; r++)
            {
                if (grid[r, c] == 0) holes++;
            }
        }

        return -(aggregateHeight * 0.51) - (holes * 0.35) - (bumpiness * 0.18);
    }

    public void ApplyMove(string pieceType, Move move)
    {
        var rotation = PieceDefinitions.Pieces[pieceType][move.Rotation];
        // For actual placement, we need to find the correct row
        int row = 0;
        while (CanPlace(grid, rotation, row + 1, move.Column)) row++;
        Place(grid, rotation, row, move.Column);
        ClearLines(grid);
    }
}
