use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let parts: Vec<usize> = first_line
        .split_whitespace()
        .map(|s| s.parse().unwrap())
        .collect();
    let n = parts[0];
    let m = parts[1];

    let mut adj = vec![vec![false; n]; n];
    for _ in 0..m {
        let line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
        let edge: Vec<usize> = line
            .split_whitespace()
            .map(|s| s.parse().unwrap())
            .collect();
        let u = edge[0];
        let v = edge[1];
        adj[u][v] = true;
        adj[v][u] = true;
    }

    let mut min_cut = usize::MAX;
    let mut best_partition = Vec::new();

    let mut current_partition = Vec::new();
    let mut used = vec![false; n];

    fn find_min_cut(
        n: usize,
        adj: &Vec<Vec<bool>>,
        k: usize,
        start: usize,
        current_partition: &mut Vec<usize>,
        used: &mut Vec<bool>,
        min_cut: &mut usize,
        best_partition: &mut Vec<usize>,
    ) {
        if current_partition.len() == n / 2 {
            let mut cut = 0;
            let mut in_partition = vec![false; n];
            for &v in current_partition.iter() {
                in_partition[v] = true;
            }

            for &u in current_partition.iter() {
                for v in 0..n {
                    if !in_partition[v] && adj[u][v] {
                        cut += 1;
                    }
                }
            }

            if cut < *min_cut {
                *min_cut = cut;
                *best_partition = current_partition.clone();
            }
            return;
        }

        for i in start..n {
            if !used[i] {
                used[i] = true;
                current_partition.push(i);
                find_min_cut(n, adj, k, i + 1, current_partition, used, min_cut, best_partition);
                current_partition.pop();
                used[i] = false;
            }
        }
    }

    find_min_cut(n, &adj, n / 2, 0, &mut current_partition, &mut used, &mut min_cut, &mut best_partition);

    println!("{}", min_cut);
    let output: Vec<String> = best_partition.iter().map(|v| v.to_string()).collect();
    println!("{}", output.join(" "));
}

View C++ Code (2054 chars)
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

// Maximum Weight Independent Set problem:
// Maximize sum(c_i * x_i) subject to x_u + x_v <= 1 for all edges (u, v).
// Since x_u + x_v <= 1 means we cannot select both u and v, this is equivalent
// to finding the Maximum Weight Independent Set in the graph defined by these constraints.

struct Solver {
    int n, m;
    vector<long long> c;
    vector<vector<int>> adj;
    
    long long max_weight = -1;
    vector<int> best_x;
    
    vector<int> current_x;
    long long current_weight = 0;

    void solve(int idx) {
        if (idx == n) {
            if (current_weight > max_weight) {
                max_weight = current_weight;
                best_x = current_x;
            }
            return;
        }

        // Try NOT selecting variable idx
        current_x[idx] = 0;
        solve(idx + 1);

        // Try selecting variable idx (if allowed)
        bool can_select = true;
        for (int neighbor : adj[idx]) {
            if (neighbor < idx && current_x[neighbor] == 1) {
                can_select = false;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (can_select) {
            current_x[idx] = 1;
            current_weight += c[idx];
            solve(idx + 1);
            current_weight -= c[idx];
            current_x[idx] = 0;
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    int n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    vector<long long> c(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> c[i];

    vector<vector<int>> adj(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        cin >> u >> v;
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    Solver solver;
    solver.n = n;
    solver.m = m;
    solver.c = c;
    solver.adj = adj;
    solver.current_x.assign(n, 0);
    solver.best_x.assign(n, 0);

    solver.solve(0);

    cout << solver.max_weight << endl;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        cout << solver.best_x[i] << (i == n - 1 ? "" : " ");
    }
    cout << endl;

    return 0;
}

%cy = OpFSub %float (OpFMul %float %uv_y %float_2) %float_1 ; uv.y*2 - 1

%zy_init = OpCopyObject %float %float_0

%iter_phi = OpPhi %int %iter_init %label_main %iter_next %loop_continue
%zx_phi = OpPhi %float %zx_init %label_main %zx_new %loop_continue
%zy_phi = OpPhi %float %zy_init %label_main %zy_new %loop_continue

OpBranchConditional %loop_cond %loop_body %loop_break

%loop_body = OpLabel
; z = z^2 + c => zx_new = zx^2 - zy^2 + cx; zy_new = 2*zx*zy + cy
%zx2 = OpFMul %float %zx_phi %zx_phi
%zy2 = OpFMul %float %zy_phi %zy_phi
%zx_new = OpFAdd %float %cx (OpFSub %float %zx2 %zy2)
%zy_new = OpFAdd %float %cy (OpFMul %float %float_2 (OpFMul %float %zx_phi %zy_phi))

%mag2_real = OpFAdd %float %zx2 %zy2
%escape = OpFOrdGreaterThan %bool %mag2_real %float_4
OpBranchConditional %escape %loop_break %loop_continue

%loop_continue = OpLabel
%iter_next = OpIAdd %int %iter_phi %int_1
OpBranch %loop_header

%loop_break = OpLabel
%iter_final = OpPhi %int %iter_phi %loop_header %iter_phi %loop_body
; Coloring
%t = OpFDiv %float (OpConvertSToF %float %iter_final) %float_20 ; iter/20
%r = OpCopyObject %float %t
%g = OpFMul %float %t %float_0_5
%b = OpFSub %float %float_1 %t
%color = OpCompositeConstruct %vec4 %r %g %b %float_1
OpStore %out_color %color
OpReturn
OpFunctionEnd

Typical Prompt:
You are writing a SPIR-V assembly geometry shader. It will be assembled with
spirv-as (Vulkan 1.0) and rendered using a fixed vertex shader and fragment shader.

**Geometry shader requirements:**
- `OpCapability Geometry`
- `OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450`
- `OpEntryPoint Geometry %main "main"` listing ALL interface variables
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (InputPoints/InputLines/Triangles/InputLinesAdjacency/InputTrianglesAdjacency)
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (OutputPoints/OutputLineStrip/OutputTriangleStrip)
- `OpExecutionMode %main OutputVertices ` (max vertices emitted)
- `OpExecutionMode %main Invocations 1`

**Input from vertex shader (per-vertex arrays):**
The input gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block (must be decorated with Block + BuiltIn Position).
```
%gl_PerVertex_in = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in 0 BuiltIn Position
; Array size depends on input primitive:
; InputPoints: 1, InputLines: 2, Triangles: 3
; InputLinesAdjacency: 4, InputTrianglesAdjacency: 6
%arr_pv_in = OpTypeArray %gl_PerVertex_in %uint_N
%ptr_in_arr_pv = OpTypePointer Input %arr_pv_in
%gl_in = OpVariable %ptr_in_arr_pv Input
; Access: OpAccessChain %ptr_in_v4 %gl_in %int_i %int_0 -> gl_in[i].gl_Position
```

User-defined inputs are also arrays of the same size:
```
layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos[]; ; positions in clip space
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal[]; ; vertex normals
layout(location = 2) in vec3 color[]; ; per-vertex colors
```

**Output (per emitted vertex):**
The output gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block:
```
%gl_PerVertex_out = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out 0 BuiltIn Position
%ptr_out_pv = OpTypePointer Output %gl_PerVertex_out
%gl_out = OpVariable %ptr_out_pv Output
; Store: OpAccessChain %ptr_out_v4 %gl_out %int_0 -> gl_out.gl_Position
```
```
layout(location = 0) out vec3 outColor; ; color for fragment shader
```

**Emit vertices with:** `OpEmitVertex` after storing gl_Position and outColor.
**End primitive with:** `OpEndPrimitive` after emitting a complete strip.

**Available UBO (set=0, binding=0) - accessible from geometry shader:**
Same layout as test 41 (model/view/proj matrices, lightPos, cameraPos, params).

**Write ONLY the complete SPIR-V assembly text for the geometry shader.**


**Input primitive:** InputPoints (1 vertex per invocation, array size 1)
**Geometry:** 25 colored points in a 5x5 grid spread across [-0.8, 0.8].

**Task:** Expand each point into a small colored quad (4 vertices as triangle strip).
1. Read gl_in[0].gl_Position (the point position).
2. Read color[0] (the point's color).
3. Define a half-size: h = 0.04.
4. Emit 4 vertices forming a quad centered on the point:
- (x-h, y-h), (x+h, y-h), (x-h, y+h), (x+h, y+h)
- All with z=0, w=1, and the same color.
5. Output as triangle strip, max 4 vertices.
 Prompt Changes:
Prompt parameters change between subpasses (increasing difficulty)

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 R = reflect(-L, N);

    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float specular = pow(max(dot(R, V), 0.0), 32.0);

    float intensity = 0.2 + 0.5 * diffuse + 0.8 * specular;

    return float4(float3(intensity, intensity, intensity), 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0
{
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 H = normalize(L + V);

    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float specular = pow(max(dot(N, H), 0.0), 64.0);

    float intensity = 0.1 + 0.6 * diffuse + 0.8 * specular;

    return float4(intensity, intensity, intensity, 1.0);
}

View HLSL (1074 chars)
struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0
{
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);

    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    
    // Base color calculation
    float3 baseColor = float3(0.2, 0.3, 0.8);
    float3 diffuseColor = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.5 * diffuse);
    
    // Rim lighting calculation
    float rim = pow(1.0 - max(dot(N, V), 0.0), 3.0);
    float3 rimTint = float3(1.0, 0.8, 0.5);
    float3 finalColor = diffuseColor + (rimTint * rim);

    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    // 1. Calculate checkerboard
    float2 grid = floor(input.uv * 8.0);
    float checker = fmod(grid.x + grid.y, 2.0);
    float3 checkerColor = lerp(float3(0.9, 0.9, 0.9), float3(0.2, 0.2, 0.2), checker);

    // 2. Lambertian Shading
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float3 shading = 0.5 + 0.5 * diffuse;

    // 3. Final color
    float3 finalColor = checkerColor * shading;
    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0
{
    // Stripe logic: sin(uv.y * PI * 16.0)
    // Red (0.9, 0.1, 0.1), Blue (0.1, 0.1, 0.9)
    float stripe = sin(input.uv.y * 3.14159 * 16.0);
    float3 baseColor = (stripe > 0.0) ? float3(0.9, 0.1, 0.1) : float3(0.1, 0.1, 0.9);

    // Lambertian shading
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float3 lighting = baseColor * (0.4 + 0.6 * diffuse);

    return float4(lighting, 1.0);
}

    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;   // per-vertex color (smoothly varies: rgb = 0.5+0.5*xyz)
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;          // offset 0   (column-major)
    float4x4 view;           // offset 64
    float4x4 projection;     // offset 128
    float4 lightPos;         // value: (5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 1.0)
    float4 cameraPos;        // value: (0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0)
    float4 params;           // value: (0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0)
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    
    // Hemisphere lighting
    float3 skyColor = float3(0.4, 0.6, 1.0);
    float3 groundColor = float3(0.3, 0.15, 0.05);
    float3 ambient = lerp(groundColor, skyColor, N.y * 0.5 + 0.5);
    
    // Diffuse lighting
    float diff = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float3 diffuse = 0.3 * diff;
    
    float3 finalColor = ambient + diffuse;
    
    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

Approach: HLSL Pixel Shader for Vulkan Rendering the Mandelbrot set

View HLSL (1330 chars)
struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;   // world-space position
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;   // world-space normal
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;   // texture coordinates in [0,1]
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;   // tangent vector
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;   // per-vertex color
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    // Map UVs [0,1] to complex plane c = (uv.x*3-2, uv.y*2-1)
    float2 c = float2(input.uv.x * 3.0 - 2.0, input.uv.y * 2.0 - 1.0);
    
    float2 z = float2(0.0, 0.0);
    float iterations = 0.0;
    const float max_iterations = 20.0;
    
    for (float i = 0.0; i < max_iterations; ++i) {
        // z = z^2 + c
        // (x+yi)^2 = x^2 - y^2 + 2xyi
        float x2 = z.x * z.x;
        float y2 = z.y * z.y;
        
        if (x2 + y2 > 4.0) break;
        
        z = float2(x2 - y2, 2.0 * z.x * z.y) + c;
        iterations += 1.0;
    }
    
    float t = iterations / max_iterations;
    
    // Coloring: (t, t*0.5, 1.0-t), alpha 1.0
    return float4(t, t * 0.5, 1.0 - t, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float2 scale = float2(8.0, 16.0);
    float2 uv = input.uv * scale;

    // Stagger rows: every other row is shifted by 0.5
    float row = floor(uv.y);
    if (fmod(row, 2.0) >= 1.0) {
        uv.x += 0.5;
    }

    float2 cell = floor(uv);
    float2 localUV = frac(uv);

    // Mortar thickness
    float2 mortar = float2(0.05, 0.1);
    
    // Check if within mortar
    bool isMortar = (localUV.x < mortar.x) || (localUV.x > 1.0 - mortar.x) ||
                    (localUV.y < mortar.y) || (localUV.y > 1.0 - mortar.y);
    
    float3 brickColor = float3(0.7, 0.2, 0.1);
    float3 mortarColor = float3(0.7, 0.7, 0.7);
    
    float3 baseColor = isMortar ? mortarColor : brickColor;
    
    // Lighting
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float shading = 0.4 + 0.6 * diffuse;
    
    return float4(baseColor * shading, 1.0);
}

layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos;   // world-space position
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal;     // world-space normal
layout(location = 2) in vec2 uv;         // texture coordinates in [0,1]
layout(location = 3) in vec3 tangent;    // tangent vector
layout(location = 4) in vec3 color;      // per-vertex color

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform UBO {
    mat4 model;          // offset 0   (column-major)
    mat4 view;           // offset 64
    mat4 projection;     // offset 128
    vec4 lightPos;       // value: (5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 1.0)
    vec4 cameraPos;      // value: (0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0)
    vec4 params;         // value: (0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0)
} ubo;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 outColor;  // RGBA float

void main() {
    // Normalize interpolated normal
    vec3 N = normalize(normal);
    // Calculate View vector
    vec3 V = normalize(ubo.cameraPos.xyz - worldPos);
    // Calculate Light vector
    vec3 L = normalize(ubo.lightPos.xyz - worldPos);

    // Diffuse
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    vec3 baseColor = vec3(0.2, 0.3, 0.8);
    vec3 diffuseComponent = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.5 * diffuse);

    // Rim (Fresnel)
    float rimFactor = pow(1.0 - max(dot(N, V), 0.0), 3.0);
    vec3 rimTint = vec3(1.0, 0.8, 0.5);
    vec3 rimComponent = rimTint * rimFactor;

    // Final Color
    outColor = vec4(diffuseComponent + rimComponent, 1.0);
}

    vec3 finalColor = baseColor * lightIntensity;
    
    outColor = vec4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

}

layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos;   // world-space position
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal;     // world-space normal (interpolated, may need normalize)
layout(location = 2) in vec2 uv;         // texture coordinates in [0,1]
layout(location = 3) in vec3 tangent;    // tangent vector
layout(location = 4) in vec3 color;      // per-vertex color (smoothly varies: rgb = 0.5+0.5*xyz)

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform UBO {
    mat4 model;          // offset 0   (column-major)
    mat4 view;           // offset 64
    mat4 projection;     // offset 128
    vec4 lightPos;       // value: (5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 1.0)
    vec4 cameraPos;      // value: (0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0)
    vec4 params;         // value: (0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0)
} ubo;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 outColor;  // RGBA float, stored as rgba8unorm

void main() {
    vec3 N = normalize(normal);
    vec3 L = normalize(ubo.lightPos.xyz - worldPos);
    
    // Lambertian lighting
    float diff = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    vec3 baseColor = vec3(0.8, 0.2, 0.2);
    vec3 shadedColor = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.7 * diff);
    
    // Distance-based fog
    float dist = length(ubo.cameraPos.xyz - worldPos);
    float fogFactor = clamp((dist - 1.5) / 3.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    vec3 fogColor = vec3(0.7, 0.7, 0.8);
    
    vec3 finalColor = mix(shadedColor, fogColor, fogFactor);
    
    outColor = vec4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

    vec2 c = vec2(uv.x * 3.0 - 2.0, uv.y * 2.0 - 1.0);
    vec2 z = vec2(0.0);
    int iterations = 0;
    
    // Mandelbrot iteration
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
        // z = z^2 + c => (x+iy)^2 + c = (x^2-y^2 + cx, 2xy + cy)
        z = vec2(z.x * z.x - z.y * z.y, 2.0 * z.x * z.y) + c;
        if (dot(z, z) > 4.0) {
            break;
        }
        iterations++;
    }
    
    // Calculate color based on iteration count
    float t = float(iterations) / 20.0;
    outColor = vec4(t, t * 0.5, 1.0 - t, 1.0);
}

You are writing a SPIR-V fragment shader as raw binary data, encoded as a hex string.
The binary will be decoded from hex, validated with spirv-val, and rendered on a unit sphere.

**SPIR-V Binary Format (little-endian 32-bit words):**
Each 32-bit word is 8 hex characters (little-endian byte order).

Header (5 words):
```
03022307 // Magic number 0x07230203 (little-endian)
00000100 // Version 1.0 (0x00010000)
00000000 // Generator (0 = manual)
BBBBBBBB // Bound (max ID + 1)
00000000 // Reserved
```

Instructions follow as: first word = (WordCount << 16) | Opcode, then operands.

**Key opcodes (decimal):**
- OpCapability (17): word_count=2, operand=capability (1=Shader)
- OpExtInstImport (11): result_id, name_string
- OpMemoryModel (14): word_count=3, addressing=0(Logical), model=1(GLSL450)
- OpEntryPoint (15): execution_model=4(Fragment), entry_id, name, interface_vars...
- OpExecutionMode (16): entry_id, mode=7(OriginUpperLeft)
- OpDecorate (71): target, decoration, operands
- OpTypeVoid (19), OpTypeFunction (33), OpTypeFloat (22), OpTypeVector (23)
- OpTypePointer (32), OpVariable (59), OpConstant (43)
- OpFunction (54), OpFunctionEnd (56), OpLabel (248)
- OpLoad (61), OpStore (62), OpReturn (253)
- OpCompositeConstruct (80), OpCompositeExtract (81)
- OpDot (148), OpFMul (133), OpFAdd (129), OpFSub (131), OpFNegate (127)

**Decoration values:** Location=30, DescriptorSet=34, Binding=33, Block=2, Offset=35

Typical Prompt:
Write a GLSL compute shader for gravitational N-body simulation.

**GLSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// Each body is stored as two consecutive vec4s:
// vec4(position.xyz, mass)
// vec4(velocity.xyz, 0.0)
// So body i starts at index i*2 in the buffer.

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer InputBodies {
vec4 inData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) buffer OutputBodies {
vec4 outData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform Params {
uvec4 counts; // counts.x = N (number of bodies)
vec4 physics; // physics.x = dt, physics.y = softening, physics.z = G
};
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that performs ONE timestep of gravitational
N-body simulation using the leapfrog/Euler integration method. Each invocation
handles one body (gl_GlobalInvocationID.x), reading its position and velocity
from inData and writing updated values to outData. The acceleration should be
computed from all other bodies using:

acc += G * mass_j * (pos_j - pos_i) / (|pos_j - pos_i|^2 + softening^2)^(3/2)

Velocity is advanced by acc * dt and position is advanced by vel * dt. The
shader will be dispatched ceil(N/256) workgroups in X and run multiple times
with ping-pong buffers for the required number of timesteps.

**Critical Requirements:**
- Guard against gl_GlobalInvocationID.x >= N
- Use the softening parameter to avoid singularities
- Skip self-interaction (i == j)
- Write BOTH position+mass and velocity vec4s to output


**Test Configurations:**
Subpass 0: N=64, timesteps=10, dt=0.001, softening=0.01
Subpass 1: N=128, timesteps=20, dt=0.001, softening=0.01
Subpass 2: N=256, timesteps=50, dt=0.001, softening=0.01
Subpass 3: N=512, timesteps=100, dt=0.001, softening=0.01
Subpass 4: N=1024, timesteps=100, dt=0.001, softening=0.01
Subpass 5: N=2048, timesteps=200, dt=0.001, softening=0.01

G = 0.006674 (scaled gravitational constant)

@group(0) @binding(2) var params : vec4;
// params.x = difficulty, params.y = range_start, params.z = range_size

fn main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid : vec3) { ... }

**Task:** Write a compute shader that searches for a uint32 nonce such that

**Hash function (MUST match exactly):**
```
function custom_hash(data[16], nonce) -> (h0, h1):
state[0..15] = data[0..15]
for i in 0..15: state[i] ^= (nonce + i)

// 8 rounds of quarter-round mixing (ChaCha-like)
repeat 8 times:
for each group of 4 consecutive elements (i, i+1, i+2, i+3):
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 16)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 12)
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 8)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 7)

// Fold 16 words to 2:
h0 = state[0] ^ state[2] ^ state[4] ^ state[6] ^ state[8] ^ state[10] ^ state[12] ^ state[14]
h1 = state[1] ^ state[3] ^ state[5] ^ state[7] ^ state[9] ^ state[11] ^ state[13] ^ state[15]
return (h0, h1) // h0 is low 32 bits
```

**Trailing zero count:** Count trailing zero bits of the 64-bit value [h0 | (h1 << 32)].
That is, count from h0's LSB first; if h0 == 0, add 32 and continue counting from h1.

**Algorithm:**
1. Each thread computes: my_nonce = params.y + gid.x (range_start + thread ID)
2. Guard: if gid.x >= params.z, return (out of range)
3. Compute hash, count trailing zeros
4. If trailing_zeros >= difficulty:
Write result[0]=1u, result[1]=nonce, result[2]=h0, result[3]=h1
(Race writes are acceptable - any valid nonce will be verified on CPU)

**Important WGSL notes:**
- Use `var state : array` for the mutable hash state.
- WGSL rotation: `(x << shift) | (x >> (32u - shift))` — all values must be u32.
- The inner quarter-round loop MUST be unrolled (write out all 4 groups
of state[0..3], state[4..7], state[8..11], state[12..15] explicitly).
- Do NOT use atomics. Plain stores to result[] are sufficient.
- All integer literals must be typed: use `0u`, `1u`, `16u`, `32u` etc.

The shader will be dispatched with ceil(range_size / 256) workgroups.
Only ONE dispatch is performed - find the nonce in a single pass.

Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V assembly compute shader for 2D Lattice Boltzmann fluid simulation.

**SPIR-V Assembly Compute Shader Interface:**

The shader uses the D2Q9 Lattice Boltzmann model for 2D fluid simulation.

**D2Q9 velocity directions (index k -> (cx, cy)):**
```
k=0: ( 0, 0) w=4/9 (rest)
k=1: ( 1, 0) w=1/9 (east)
k=2: ( 0, 1) w=1/9 (north)
k=3: (-1, 0) w=1/9 (west)
k=4: ( 0,-1) w=1/9 (south)
k=5: ( 1, 1) w=1/36 (NE)
k=6: (-1, 1) w=1/36 (NW)
k=7: (-1,-1) w=1/36 (SW)
k=8: ( 1,-1) w=1/36 (SE)
```

**Buffer layout:**
- Binding 0 (storage, read-only): float array, length W*H*9
Index = (y * W + x) * 9 + k
- Binding 1 (storage, read-write): float array, length W*H*9 (output, NOT writeonly)
- Binding 2 (uniform): { uvec4(W, H, 0, 0), vec4(omega, 0, 0, 0) }

**Algorithm (per cell at gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy):**
Compute one LBM step (collision + streaming) for each lattice cell. Guard against
out-of-bounds (x >= W or y >= H). For the cell distributions f[0..8], compute
macroscopic density rho and velocity (ux, uy) using the D2Q9 directions. Apply
the BGK collision update with:

cu = cx[k]*ux + cy[k]*uy
feq = w[k] * rho * (1 + 3*cu + 4.5*cu*cu - 1.5*(ux*ux + uy*uy))
f_out = f[k] + omega * (feq - f[k])

Then stream each f_out to the neighbor cell (x+cx[k], y+cy[k]) with periodic
wraparound in both axes. Write to the output buffer at the corresponding
neighbor index for k.

**SPIR-V requirements:**
- OpCapability Shader
- OpExecutionMode with LocalSize 16 16 1
- Use gl_GlobalInvocationID for (x, y)
- Declare runtime arrays for storage buffers with OpDecorate ArrayStride 4
- Use OpSMod or manual modulo for periodic boundary conditions

Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V binary compute shader (hex-encoded) for parallel inclusive prefix sum.

**SPIR-V Binary (hex-encoded) Compute Shader Interface:**

You must produce raw SPIR-V binary encoded as a hex string (no spaces, no 0x prefix).
The binary must start with the SPIR-V magic number 0x07230203.

**Required layout:**
```
Binding 0 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-only) - uint array, length N
Binding 1 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-write) - uint array, length N
Binding 2 (set=0): Uniform buffer - uint4: [N, 0, 0, 0]

Local size: 256 x 1 x 1
```

**Algorithm:** Inclusive prefix sum (scan)
- Input: [a0, a1, a2, a3, ...]
- Output: [a0, a0+a1, a0+a1+a2, a0+a1+a2+a3, ...]

Compute an inclusive scan over the input array. For N <= 256, use a shared-memory
scan within a single workgroup (synchronize as needed). For N > 256, a naive
fallback (each thread sums all previous elements) is acceptable but slow; full
marks require a multi-workgroup scan.

**SPIR-V binary encoding notes:**
- Little-endian uint32 words
- Magic: 0x07230203
- Version: 0x00010000 (1.0)
- Bound: upper bound on all IDs used + 1
- Schema: 0
- OpCapability Shader = [0x00020011, 0x00000001]
- OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450 = [0x00030006, 0x00000001, 0x00000001]
- OpEntryPoint GLCompute = opcode 0x0000000F, execution model 5
- OpExecutionMode LocalSize = opcode 0x00000010, mode 17 (LocalSize)
- OpDecorate Binding = decoration 33
- OpDecorate DescriptorSet = decoration 34
- OpDecorate ArrayStride = decoration 6
- OpDecorate BufferBlock or Block = decoration 2 or 3
- OpTypeInt 32 0 = unsigned int
- OpTypePointer StorageBuffer = storage class 12
- OpVariable StorageBuffer = storage class 12

Encode every uint32 word as exactly 8 hex characters (little-endian).

Subpass 1: N=1,024 elements
Subpass 2: N=4,096 elements
Subpass 3: N=16,384 elements

Each uint32 word must be 8 hex digits, little-endian byte order.

Key facts:
- Wheel speed sensors (4): FL, FR, RL, RR in km/h. Any can fail.
- Gyroscopes (3): yaw rate in degrees/second. Any can fail silently.
- Accelerometers (3): longitudinal and lateral in m/s². Any can fail.
- GPS (2): position in meters, speed in km/h. Can lose signal.
- Lidar (12 beams): range in meters at angles from -90° to +90°.
- Vision (3 independent systems): lane line distances, types (solid/dashed),
obstacle detection (bool + distance + relative speed), speed limit signs,
lane offset, road curvature. ANY can fail or flicker!
- `estimated_mu`: estimated tire-road friction (1.0=dry, <0.3=ice).
- `target_speed_kmh`: desired speed. `target_lane`: desired lane (0-2).
- `*_valid` flags exist but may be WRONG on failed sensors.
- Sensors can FLICKER: randomly return invalid data for a few frames.

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
steering: -1.0 (full left) to +1.0 (full right)
0.0 = straight ahead
throttle: 0.0 (no power) to 1.0 (full power)
brake: 0.0 (no brake) to 1.0 (emergency stop)
```
If you omit a key, the current value is maintained.

**Critical Design Requirements:**
1. **Sensor fusion**: Cross-check redundant sensors. Median/voting for disagreements.
2. **Lane keeping**: Stay centered in lane using vision line distances and lidar.
3. **Speed control**: Maintain target speed, respect speed limits.
4. **Obstacle avoidance**: If obstacle detected, brake and/or lane change.
5. **Traction management**: On low-mu surfaces, reduce speed, gentler inputs.
6. **Graceful degradation**: Handle sensor failures, flickering data.
7. **Persistence**: Module-level variables persist across calls for filtering/PID.

Test 53: Spacecraft Orbital Docking Autopilot (Python) Score: 0.00 / 25
Typical Prompt:
Write a Python autopilot to dock a spacecraft with a space station in orbit.

**CRITICAL ORBITAL MECHANICS INSIGHT:**
In orbit, relative motion is COUNTER-INTUITIVE:
- Thrusting TOWARD the target (prograde if behind) raises your orbit → you SLOW DOWN relative to target
- To catch up: thrust RETROGRADE (backward!) to lower orbit → you go FASTER
- Radial thrusts cause oscillation, not direct movement
- Cross-track corrections require thrusts at specific orbital positions
- Near the target (<50m), approximate as linear (CW equations work)
- Far away (>200m), full orbital mechanics dominate

**Function Signature:**
```python
def autopilot_step(state: dict, dt: float) -> dict:
```

Key sensor notes:
- Relative position/velocity in LVLH frame: x=radial (up), y=along-track (velocity dir), z=cross-track
- NEGATIVE y = behind station (most common start). Must CLOSE the y gap.
- Range finders give scalar distance. Radar/lidar give 3D relative pos/vel.
- All sensors can fail silently! Cross-check redundant sensors.
- Docking camera only active within 500m. Gives bearing to docking port.
- Ground station data updates every ~30s (stale but reliable).

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
thrust_x: -1.0 to +1.0 (radial: + = away from Earth)
thrust_y: -1.0 to +1.0 (along-track: + = prograde)
thrust_z: -1.0 to +1.0 (cross-track: + = north)
att_rate_roll: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_pitch: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_yaw: rad/s (max ±0.035)
```
Each thrust axis: 220N per thruster, Isp=290s. Fuel is LIMITED (~500 kg).

**Docking Success Criteria:**
- Range < 2m AND relative speed < 0.3 m/s

**Approach Strategy Hints:**
1. Far (>200m): Use Hohmann-like transfer — retrograde to lower orbit if behind
2. Medium (50-200m): Gentle corrections, V-bar approach preferred
3. Close (<50m): Linear regime, direct thrust corrections OK
4. Final (<10m): Very gentle, < 0.1 m/s approach speed

**ILS Approach Key Concepts:**
- `glideslope_N_dots`: deviation from 3° glideslope (+above/-below), 3 receivers
- `localizer_N_dots`: deviation from runway centerline (+right/-left), 3 receivers
- `radio_alt_ft`: height above ground (critical for flare)
- `dme_N_nm`: distance to runway threshold
- `weight_on_wheels`: True when landed
- `target_vref_kt`: reference approach speed (typically 137kt)
- `decision_height_ft`: minimum altitude to continue approach (200ft CAT I)
- Elevator command 0 = trimmed flight. Positive = pitch up.

**Output:** Return a dict with any of:
```
elevator: -1.0 (nose down) to +1.0 (nose up), relative to trim
aileron: -1.0 (roll left) to +1.0 (roll right)
rudder: -1.0 (yaw left) to +1.0 (yaw right)
throttle_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine)
throttle_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine)
elevator_trim: -1.0 to +1.0
flaps: degrees (0-40)
gear: 0.0 (up) or 1.0 (down)
speedbrake: 0.0 (retracted) to 1.0 (full)
spoiler: 0.0 or 1.0 (ground spoilers, deploy after touchdown)
autobrake: 0.0 to 1.0 (braking force after touchdown)
reverse_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine reverse thrust)
reverse_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine reverse thrust)
```

**Approach Phases:**
1. **Intercept** (>1000ft): Track glideslope and localizer, configure for landing
2. **Approach** (1000ft-200ft): Stabilise on glideslope, speed, config
3. **Flare** (<50ft radio alt): Reduce descent rate, idle thrust
4. **Touchdown & Rollout**: Deploy spoilers, reverse thrust, autobrake

**Go-Around:**
If the approach is unstable or unsafe, abort the landing:
- Apply TOGA thrust (throttle 1.0), pitch up, retract speedbrake
- Climb to 1500ft AGL — this completes the go-around
- The sim will then **restart** from a stable approach position with the
**same failures and weather**. Your autopilot must land on the retry.
- Each go-around costs a **0.1 point penalty** on a perfect landing.
- After **10 go-arounds** the scenario fails (score 0.0).

**Scoring:**
- **1.0** — Normal landing: stopped on the runway, or slowed below 50kt
with >30% runway remaining (pilot takes over to taxi).
Minus 0.1 per go-around.
- **0.5** — Hard landing: touchdown vertical speed 360–600 fpm.
Aircraft needs inspection but is reusable, everyone walks away.
- **0.1** — Minor overrun: aircraft rolls off the end but is caught by the
EMAS arrestor bed (within 150m past runway end). Everyone safe,
aircraft damaged.
- **0.0** — Catastrophic: touchdown >600 fpm, major overrun
beyond EMAS, runway excursion, CFIT, or failure to land. Write-off or
loss of life.

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. Normal ILS approach CAT I
1. Short final — 3nm
2. High on glideslope
3. Low on glideslope
4. Offset from centerline
5. Single engine failure on final [Kegworth (1989) / BA 38 (2008)]
6. Windshear on short final [Delta 191 (1985)]
7. Strong crosswind — 25kt
8. Gusty crosswind — 15kt gusting 30
9. CAT III low visibility
10. Slippery wet runway [Overruns at LGA, MDW]
11. Icy runway
12. Glideslope receiver 1+2 failed
13. Localizer 1 stuck + 2 biased
14. All radar altimeters failed
15. Elevator partially jammed
16. Aileron stuck 5° left
17. Unstabilised — too fast
18. Heavy weight landing
19. Asymmetric flap extension
20. Dual engine failure — glide approach [Gimli Glider (1983) / US Airways 1549 (2009)]
21. Missed approach required
22. Severe turbulence on final
23. ILS signal flickering
24. Engine failure + crosswind + wet runway [Multiple incidents]

Your single autopilot function must handle ALL scenarios.
Persistence: module-level variables persist across calls within a scenario,
but are **reset** between scenarios and between go-around attempts.

Test 55: Can your write a chess bot? (C++) Score: 0.00 / 40
Typical Prompt:
Write a C++ chess bot that for any given chess position, returns the best move to make (or the best
move you can find before the timeout).

You receive the chess position as a string in FEN notation, and you must return the move in
disambiguated algebraic notation (including the starting square, piece type, and destination square).

See:
- https://www.chess.com/terms/fen-chess

Here is an example FEN representing the starting position with white to move:
```
rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1
```

Here is an example disambiguated algebraic move:
```
pe2e4
```
This represents the king's pawn opening - moving the pawn from e2 to e4.

**Move notation rules:**
- Piece letter (lowercase p for pawn, uppercase N/B/R/Q/K for others) + source square + destination square.
- Use "x" between source and destination for captures: `pe4xd5`
- Promotion: append `/` and the piece letter, e.g. `pe7e8/Q`
- Castling: `O-O` (kingside) or `O-O-O` (queenside).
- En passant: append `ep`, e.g. `pe5xd6ep`
- Check: append `+`, e.g. `Bb4c5+`
- Checkmate: append `#`, e.g. `Qd1h5#`

**Input format (stdin, two lines):**
```
timeout_in_seconds
fen_string
```

**Output format (stdout, one line):**
```
move_in_disambiguated_algebraic
```

timeout_in_seconds will be at least 5. Your code will be compiled with full optimisations and
run on a machine with multiple cores, so threading is encouraged.

**Environment:**
Platform: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200)
Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD
Core count: 64
Memory: 127.87 GB
SIMD: AVX, AVX2, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, SSSE3
SIMD detail: AVX=yes, AVX-512F=no, AVX2=yes, SSE=yes, SSE2=yes, SSE3=yes, SSE4.1=yes, SSE4.2=yes, SSSE3=yes

**C++ Compiler:**
MSVC cl 19.50.35730 | std=c++20 (/std:c++20)

Be sure that any deviation from the C++ standard library is supported by the given compiler,
as referencing the wrong intrinsics or non-standard header (like 'bits/stdc++.h') could fail your submission.

const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
  const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  if (!input) return;
  const data = JSON.parse(input);
  const { depot, truckCount, packages } = data;

  if (packages.length === 0) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ routes: Array(truckCount).fill([]) }));
    return;
  }

  // 1. Group packages by proximity to minimize initial cluster distances
  // Simple approach: Sort by angle relative to depot (polar coordinate clustering)
  const packagesWithAngle = packages.map(pkg => ({
    ...pkg,
    angle: Math.atan2(pkg.y - depot[1], pkg.x - depot[0])
  }));

  packagesWithAngle.sort((a, b) => a.angle - b.angle);

  const routes = Array.from({ length: truckCount }, () => []);

  // Distribute packages among trucks
  for (let i = 0; i < packagesWithAngle.length; i++) {
    routes[i % truckCount].push(packagesWithAngle[i]);
  }

  // 2. Within each route, optimize using nearest neighbor
  const optimizedRoutes = routes.map(routePackages => {
    if (routePackages.length === 0) return [];

    const orderedIds = [];
    let currentPos = { x: depot[0], y: depot[1] };
    const remaining = [...routePackages];

    while (remaining.length > 0) {
      let nearestIdx = 0;
      let minDistance = Infinity;

      for (let i = 0; i < remaining.length; i++) {
        const dist = Math.sqrt(
          Math.pow(remaining[i].x - currentPos.x, 2) +
          Math.pow(remaining[i].y - currentPos.y, 2)
        );
        if (dist < minDistance) {
          minDistance = dist;
          nearestIdx = i;
        }
      }

      const next = remaining.splice(nearestIdx, 1)[0];
      orderedIds.push(next.id);
      currentPos = { x: next.x, y: next.y };
    }

    return orderedIds;
  });

  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ routes: optimizedRoutes }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
  const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  const data = JSON.parse(input);

  const { width, height, grid, ignitions, towns, cutBudget } = data;
  const gridArr = grid.map(row => row.split(''));

  // Simple greedy approach:
  // 1. Simulate fire spread without breaks to identify paths.
  // 2. Identify critical cells that lead to high-value towns.
  // 3. Place firebreaks on those cells until budget is met.

  // NOTE: This is a placeholder for the actual greedy logic.
  // Given the complexity of the problem, a full simulation is required.

  function getNeighbors(x, y) {
    const neighbors = [];
    if (x > 0) neighbors.push([x - 1, y]);
    if (x < width - 1) neighbors.push([x + 1, y]);
    if (y > 0) neighbors.push([x, y - 1]);
    if (y < height - 1) neighbors.push([x, y + 1]);
    return neighbors;
  }

  // 1. Simulate fire spread to calculate 'burn time' for each cell
  const burnTime = Array.from({ length: height }, () => Array(width).fill(Infinity));
  const queue = [];

  for (const [x, y] of ignitions) {
    if (gridArr[y][x] === '.') {
      burnTime[y][x] = 0;
      queue.push([x, y]);
    }
  }

  let head = 0;
  while (head < queue.length) {
    const [x, y] = queue[head++];
    for (const [nx, ny] of getNeighbors(x, y)) {
      if (gridArr[ny][nx] === '.' && burnTime[ny][nx] === Infinity) {
        burnTime[ny][nx] = burnTime[y][x] + 1;
        queue.push([nx, ny]);
      }
    }
  }

  // 2. Identify critical cells that burn early and are near valuable towns
  const candidates = [];
  for (const town of towns) {
    const { x, y, value } = town;
    // Look at cells around the town
    for (const [nx, ny] of [[x, y], ...getNeighbors(x, y)]) {
        if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && gridArr[ny][nx] === '.' && burnTime[ny][nx] < Infinity) {
            candidates.push({ x: nx, y: ny, time: burnTime[ny][nx], value });
        }
    }
  }

  // Sort candidates: prioritize those that burn early and are near high-value towns
  candidates.sort((a, b) => a.time - b.time || b.value - a.value);

  // 3. Select top candidates for firebreaks
  const firebreaksSet = new Set();
  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (firebreaksSet.size >= cutBudget) break;
    firebreaksSet.add(`${candidate.x},${candidate.y}`);
  }

  const firebreaks = Array.from(firebreaksSet).map(s => s.split(',').map(Number));

  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ firebreaks }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');

/**
 * Calculates shortest path distance using BFS on the grid.
 * Grid is '.' for open, '#' for blocked.
 */
function getShortestPath(grid, start, end) {
  const rows = grid.length;
  const cols = grid[0].length;
  const queue = [[start.x, start.y, 0]]; // [x, y, dist]
  const visited = new Set();
  visited.add(`${start.x},${start.y}`);

  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const [x, y, dist] = queue.shift();

    if (x === end.x && y === end.y) {
      return dist;
    }

    const neighbors = [
      [x + 1, y], [x - 1, y], [x, y + 1], [x, y - 1]
    ];

    for (const [nx, ny] of neighbors) {
      if (nx >= 0 && nx < rows && ny >= 0 && ny < cols &&
          grid[nx][ny] === '.' && !visited.has(`${nx},${ny}`)) {
        visited.add(`${nx},${ny}`);
        queue.push([nx, ny, dist + 1]);
      }
    }
  }
  return Infinity; // Should not happen based on problem constraints
}

function solve() {
  const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  const { grid, robots, jobs } = JSON.parse(input);

  // Precompute distances between every robot and every job
  const distances = robots.map(robot =>
    jobs.map(job => getShortestPath(grid, {x: robot.x, y: robot.y}, {x: job.x, y: job.y}))
  );

  const assignments = robots.map(() => []);
  const remainingJobs = new Set(jobs.map((_, index) => index));

  // Greedy assignment: assign closest available job to robots iteratively
  while (remainingJobs.size > 0) {
    for (let i = 0; i < robots.length; i++) {
      let bestJobIdx = -1;
      let minDistance = Infinity;

      for (const jobIdx of remainingJobs) {
        if (distances[i][jobIdx] < minDistance) {
          minDistance = distances[i][jobIdx];
          bestJobIdx = jobIdx;
        }
      }

      if (bestJobIdx !== -1) {
        assignments[i].push(jobs[bestJobIdx].id);
        remainingJobs.delete(bestJobIdx);
      }
    }
  }

  console.log(JSON.stringify({ assignments: assignments.map(robotJobs => robotJobs.map(j => j)) }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');

/**
 * Solves the drone pathfinding problem using a greedy approach.
 * Each drone, at each step, looks for the best immediate local reward
 * while staying within bounds and avoiding obstacles.
 */
function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(input);

    const { probability, drones, maxStepsPerDrone } = data;
    const height = probability.length;
    const width = probability[0].length;

    const visited = new Set();
    const paths = [];

    // Initialize visited for starting positions
    drones.forEach(d => {
        visited.add(`${d.x},${d.y}`);
    });

    for (const drone of drones) {
        let { x, y } = drone;
        const path = [[x, y]];

        for (let step = 0; step < maxStepsPerDrone; step++) {
            let bestMove = { dx: 0, dy: 0 };
            let maxReward = -Infinity;

            // Possible moves: stay, up, down, left, right
            const moves = [
                { dx: 0, dy: 0 },
                { dx: 0, dy: -1 },
                { dx: 0, dy: 1 },
                { dx: -1, dy: 0 },
                { dx: 1, dy: 0 }
            ];

            for (const move of moves) {
                const nextX = x + move.dx;
                const nextY = y + move.dy;

                // Check bounds and obstacles
                if (nextX >= 0 && nextX < width && nextY >= 0 && nextY < height &&
                    probability[nextY][nextX] !== -1) {
                    
                    // Simple greedy heuristic: probability of next cell
                    // If already visited, reward is 0
                    let reward = 0;
                    if (!visited.has(`${nextX},${nextY}`)) {
                        reward = probability[nextY][nextX];
                    }

                    if (reward > maxReward) {
                        maxReward = reward;
                        bestMove = move;
                    }
                }
            }

            x += bestMove.dx;
            y += bestMove.dy;
            path.push([x, y]);
            visited.add(`${x},${y}`);
        }
        paths.push(path);
    }

    console.log(JSON.stringify({ paths }));
}

solve();

Space Mission Work Schedule - 24 tasks, 3 workstations

View JavaScript code (2571 chars)
const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
  const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  const { machineCount, tasks } = JSON.parse(input);

  // Build dependency graph and in-degree map
  const adj = new Map();
  const inDegree = new Map();
  const taskMap = new Map();
  
  for (const task of tasks) {
    adj.set(task.id, []);
    inDegree.set(task.id, 0);
    taskMap.set(task.id, task);
  }

  for (const task of tasks) {
    for (const depId of task.deps) {
      adj.get(depId).push(task.id);
      inDegree.set(task.id, inDegree.get(task.id) + 1);
    }
  }

  // Priority queue (simple array for this prototype, sorted by weighted deadline)
  // Heuristic: prioritize tasks with earlier deadlines and higher weights
  const getPriority = (taskId) => {
    const task = taskMap.get(taskId);
    // Lower score is higher priority: weight/deadline ratio or deadline-weight
    return task.deadline - task.weight;
  };

  const readyTasks = [];
  for (const task of tasks) {
    if (inDegree.get(task.id) === 0) {
      readyTasks.push(task.id);
    }
  }
  readyTasks.sort((a, b) => getPriority(a) - getPriority(b));

  const schedule = [];
  const machines = new Array(machineCount).fill(0); // machine free time
  const taskFinishes = new Map(); // when each task finishes

  while (readyTasks.length > 0) {
    const taskId = readyTasks.shift();
    const task = taskMap.get(taskId);

    // Calculate start time: max(dependency finish times, machine free time)
    let startTime = 0;
    for (const depId of task.deps) {
      startTime = Math.max(startTime, taskFinishes.get(depId));
    }
    
    // Find earliest available machine
    let bestMachine = 0;
    let minMachineTime = machines[0];
    for (let i = 1; i < machineCount; i++) {
        if (machines[i] < minMachineTime) {
            minMachineTime = machines[i];
            bestMachine = i;
        }
    }
    
    startTime = Math.max(startTime, minMachineTime);
    
    // Schedule task
    schedule.push({
      id: taskId,
      start: startTime,
      machine: bestMachine
    });
    
    const finishTime = startTime + task.duration;
    taskFinishes.set(taskId, finishTime);
    machines[bestMachine] = finishTime;

    // Update ready tasks
    for (const neighborId of adj.get(taskId)) {
      inDegree.set(neighborId, inDegree.get(neighborId) - 1);
      if (inDegree.get(neighborId) === 0) {
        readyTasks.push(neighborId);
      }
    }
    readyTasks.sort((a, b) => getPriority(a) - getPriority(b));
  }

  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ schedule }));
}

solve();

declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

interface Point {
    x: number;
    y: number;
}

interface Package {
    id: number;
    x: number;
    y: number;
}

interface InputData {
    depot: Point;
    truckCount: number;
    packages: Package[];
}

function distance(p1: Point, p2: Point): number {
    return Math.sqrt(Math.pow(p1.x - p2.x, 2) + Math.pow(p1.y - p2.y, 2));
}

function solve() {
    const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);

    const depot = data.depot;
    const truckCount = data.truckCount;
    const unvisitedPackages = [...data.packages];
    const routes: number[][] = Array.from({ length: truckCount }, () => []);

    // Greedy heuristic: Assign packages to trucks based on nearest neighbor 
    // to the last package in their current route (or depot if empty).

    while (unvisitedPackages.length > 0) {
        for (let i = 0; i < truckCount && unvisitedPackages.length > 0; i++) {
            const route = routes[i];
            const lastLocation = route.length === 0 ? depot : data.packages.find(p => p.id === route[route.length - 1])!;
            
            let nearestIdx = 0;
            let minDistance = Infinity;

            for (let j = 0; j < unvisitedPackages.length; j++) {
                const dist = distance(lastLocation, unvisitedPackages[j]);
                if (dist < minDistance) {
                    minDistance = dist;
                    nearestIdx = j;
                }
            }

            const packageToVisit = unvisitedPackages.splice(nearestIdx, 1)[0];
            route.push(packageToVisit.id);
        }
    }

    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ routes }));
}

solve();

Wildfire Firebreak Planner - 32x22 forest, 3 towns

View TypeScript code (3114 chars)
declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

interface Town {
    id: string;
    x: number;
    y: number;
    value: number;
}

interface InputData {
    width: number;
    height: number;
    grid: string[];
    ignitions: [number, number][];
    towns: Town[];
    cutBudget: number;
}

function solve() {
    const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);
    const { width, height, grid, ignitions, towns, cutBudget } = data;

    // Use BFS to find the distance from the nearest ignition source to every cell
    const dist = Array.from({ length: height }, () => Array(width).fill(Infinity));
    const queue: [number, number][] = [];

    for (const [ix, iy] of ignitions) {
        dist[iy][ix] = 0;
        queue.push([ix, iy]);
    }

    let head = 0;
    while (head < queue.length) {
        const [x, y] = queue[head++];
        const d = dist[y][x];

        const dirs = [[0, 1], [0, -1], [1, 0], [-1, 0]];
        for (const [dx, dy] of dirs) {
            const nx = x + dx, ny = y + dy;
            if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && grid[ny][nx] === '.' && dist[ny][nx] === Infinity) {
                dist[ny][nx] = d + 1;
                queue.push([nx, ny]);
            }
        }
    }

    // Sort towns by distance from fire, then by value (descending)
    const sortedTowns = [...towns].sort((a, b) => {
        const distA = dist[a.y][a.x];
        const distB = dist[b.y][b.x];
        if (distA !== distB) return distA - distB;
        return b.value - a.value;
    });

    const firebreaks: [number, number][] = [];
    let cutsRemaining = cutBudget;
    const cutSet = new Set<string>();

    // For each town, try to cut a path
    for (const town of sortedTowns) {
        if (cutsRemaining <= 0) break;
        if (dist[town.y][town.x] === Infinity) continue; // Already unreachable or safe

        // Trace back path from town to ignition
        let curr: [number, number] = [town.x, town.y];
        while (dist[curr[1]][curr[0]] > 0) {
            if (cutsRemaining <= 0) break;

            const [x, y] = curr;
            let bestNext: [number, number] = curr;
            let minD = dist[y][x];

            const dirs = [[0, 1], [0, -1], [1, 0], [-1, 0]];
            for (const [dx, dy] of dirs) {
                const nx = x + dx, ny = y + dy;
                if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && dist[ny][nx] < minD) {
                    minD = dist[ny][nx];
                    bestNext = [nx, ny];
                }
            }

            // Cut the current cell (if it's not the town itself)
            if (bestNext !== curr) {
                const key = `${curr[0]},${curr[1]}`;
                if (!cutSet.has(key)) {
                    firebreaks.push(curr);
                    cutSet.add(key);
                    cutsRemaining--;
                }
                curr = bestNext;
            } else {
                break; // Should not happen
            }
        }
    }

    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ firebreaks }));
}

solve();

Warehouse Robot Job Planner - 28 jobs, 2 robots

View TypeScript code (2362 chars)
const fs = require('fs');

interface Robot {
  id: number;
  x: number;
  y: number;
}

interface Job {
  id: number;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  priority: number;
}

interface InputData {
  grid: string[];
  robots: Robot[];
  jobs: Job[];
}

function solve() {
  const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);
  const { grid, robots, jobs } = data;

  const rows = grid.length;
  const cols = grid[0].length;

  // BFS to find shortest path distances
  function getDistances(startX: number, startY: number): number[][] {
    const dists: number[][] = Array.from({ length: rows }, () => Array(cols).fill(-1));
    const queue: [number, number, number][] = [[startX, startY, 0]];
    dists[startY][startX] = 0;

    while (queue.length > 0) {
      const [x, y, d] = queue.shift()!;
      
      const neighbors = [
        [x + 1, y], [x - 1, y], [x, y + 1], [x, y - 1]
      ];

      for (const [nx, ny] of neighbors) {
        if (nx >= 0 && nx < cols && ny >= 0 && ny < rows && grid[ny][nx] === '.' && dists[ny][nx] === -1) {
          dists[ny][nx] = d + 1;
          queue.push([nx, ny, d + 1]);
        }
      }
    }
    return dists;
  }

  // Calculate distances from all robots to all jobs
  const robotDistances = robots.map(r => getDistances(r.x, r.y));

  // Greedily assign jobs based on priority and proximity
  const assignments: number[][] = Array.from({ length: robots.length }, () => []);
  const unassignedJobs = new Set(jobs);

  while (unassignedJobs.size > 0) {
    let bestJob: Job | null = null;
    let bestRobotIdx = -1;
    let minDistance = Infinity;

    for (const job of unassignedJobs) {
      for (let i = 0; i < robots.length; i++) {
        const dist = robotDistances[i][job.y][job.x];
        if (dist !== -1) {
          // Heuristic: prioritize high priority and short distance
          // Simple greedy: pick job that is closest to any robot
          if (dist < minDistance) {
            minDistance = dist;
            bestJob = job;
            bestRobotIdx = i;
          }
        }
      }
    }

    if (bestJob) {
      assignments[bestRobotIdx].push(bestJob.id);
      unassignedJobs.delete(bestJob);
    } else {
      // Should not happen if all jobs are reachable
      break;
    }
  }

  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ assignments }));
}

solve();

Write a complete Node.js TypeScript program for this benchmark task.

Plan grid paths for search drones.

The input JSON contains:
- `probability`: 2D array; -1 is an obstacle, positive values are search value
- `drones`: starting cells `{id, x, y}`
- `maxStepsPerDrone`

Return JSON:
```
{"paths": [[[x,y], [x,y], ...], ...]}
```
Each path belongs to the drone with the same index. Moves must be up/down/left/right
or stay in place, must stay inside the grid, and must avoid obstacles. The score is
unique probability covered compared with a greedy reference search.

Drone Search Coverage Planner - 2 drones, 55 steps

View TypeScript code (2637 chars)
declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

interface Drone {
    id: number;
    x: number;
    y: number;
}

interface InputData {
    probability: number[][];
    drones: Drone[];
    maxStepsPerDrone: number;
}

interface OutputData {
    paths: [number, number][][];
}

function solve() {
    const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);

    const { probability, drones, maxStepsPerDrone } = data;
    const height = probability.length;
    const width = probability[0].length;

    // Keep track of visited cells (to avoid double counting in score)
    // Actually, the problem says "score is unique probability covered",
    // implying if two drones cover the same cell, it only counts once.
    // For greedy, we can use a local 'covered' grid.
    const covered = Array.from({ length: height }, () => Array(width).fill(false));

    const paths: [number, number][][] = drones.map(() => []);

    // Current positions of drones
    const currentPositions = drones.map(d => ({ x: d.x, y: d.y }));

    // Initialize paths with starting positions
    for (let i = 0; i < drones.length; i++) {
        paths[i].push([currentPositions[i].x, currentPositions[i].y]);
        covered[currentPositions[i].y][currentPositions[i].x] = true;
    }

    // Directions: Stay, Up, Down, Left, Right
    const moves = [
        [0, 0], [0, -1], [0, 1], [-1, 0], [1, 0]
    ];

    for (let step = 0; step < maxStepsPerDrone; step++) {
        for (let i = 0; i < drones.length; i++) {
            let bestMove = { dx: 0, dy: 0 };
            let maxGain = -1;

            const { x, y } = currentPositions[i];

            for (const [dx, dy] of moves) {
                const nx = x + dx;
                const ny = y + dy;

                if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && probability[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                    let gain = 0;
                    if (!covered[ny][nx]) {
                        gain = probability[ny][nx];
                    }

                    if (gain > maxGain) {
                        maxGain = gain;
                        bestMove = { dx, dy };
                    }
                }
            }

            // Apply best move
            currentPositions[i].x += bestMove.dx;
            currentPositions[i].y += bestMove.dy;
            
            paths[i].push([currentPositions[i].x, currentPositions[i].y]);
            covered[currentPositions[i].y][currentPositions[i].x] = true;
        }
    }

    const output: OutputData = { paths };
    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(output));
}

solve();

import * as fs from 'fs';

interface Task {
  id: string;
  duration: number;
  deps: string[];
  deadline: number;
  weight: number;
}

interface InputData {
  machineCount: number;
  tasks: Task[];
}

interface ScheduleEntry {
  id: string;
  start: number;
  machine: number;
}

function solve() {
  const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
  const data: InputData = JSON.parse(input);

  const { machineCount, tasks } = data;

  // Build graph
  const taskMap = new Map<string, Task>();
  const adj = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const inDegree = new Map<string, number>();

  for (const task of tasks) {
    taskMap.set(task.id, task);
    if (!adj.has(task.id)) adj.set(task.id, []);
    if (!inDegree.has(task.id)) inDegree.set(task.id, 0);
  }

  for (const task of tasks) {
    for (const dep of task.deps) {
      if (!adj.has(dep)) adj.set(dep, []);
      adj.get(dep)!.push(task.id);
      inDegree.set(task.id, (inDegree.get(task.id) || 0) + 1);
    }
  }

  // List Scheduling
  const readyQueue: string[] = [];
  for (const [id, degree] of inDegree.entries()) {
    if (degree === 0) readyQueue.push(id);
  }

  const machineAvailableTime: number[] = new Array(machineCount).fill(0);
  const taskFinishTime = new Map<string, number>();
  const schedule: ScheduleEntry[] = [];

  // Simple heuristic: sort ready queue by deadline or weight
  // For now: just process in order
  
  while (readyQueue.length > 0) {
    // Sort ready tasks by a simple heuristic: e.g., earliest deadline first
    readyQueue.sort((a, b) => {
        const taskA = taskMap.get(a)!;
        const taskB = taskMap.get(b)!;
        return taskA.deadline - taskB.deadline;
    });

    const taskId = readyQueue.shift()!;
    const task = taskMap.get(taskId)!;

    // Find earliest start time based on dependencies
    let startTime = 0;
    for (const depId of task.deps) {
      startTime = Math.max(startTime, taskFinishTime.get(depId) || 0);
    }

    // Find earliest available machine
    let bestMachine = 0;
    let minFinish = Infinity;
    
    // We want the machine that can start the task earliest.
    // That's min(max(startTime, machineAvailableTime[m]))
    
    let earliestPossibleStart = Infinity;
    for (let m = 0; m < machineCount; m++) {
        const potentialStart = Math.max(startTime, machineAvailableTime[m]);
        if (potentialStart < earliestPossibleStart) {
            earliestPossibleStart = potentialStart;
            bestMachine = m;
        }
    }

    const start = earliestPossibleStart;
    schedule.push({ id: taskId, start, machine: bestMachine });
    const finish = start + task.duration;
    taskFinishTime.set(taskId, finish);
    machineAvailableTime[bestMachine] = finish;

    // Update dependents
    for (const neighbor of (adj.get(taskId) || [])) {
      inDegree.set(neighbor, inDegree.get(neighbor)! - 1);
      if (inDegree.get(neighbor) === 0) {
        readyQueue.push(neighbor);
      }
    }
  }

  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ schedule }));
}

solve();
